work: A Survey of World Model Benchmarks
method: Surveys 102 representative benchmarks and organizes evaluation by capability target, protocol, metric family and data source.
evidence: World-model evaluation is already a broad, rapidly formalizing benchmark field; metric/protocol claims need precise coordinates.
limitation: Does not identify mechanic-controlled planning-burden-matched instance synthesis as an occupied benchmark class in the current audit.

work: Distributionally Robust Games via Coherent Risk Measures
area: Robust game theory / distributional uncertainty / equilibrium
method: Studies strategic games where payoff distributions are uncertain and players use distributionally robust/coherent-risk objectives; develops equilibrium existence/complexity/formulations and evaluates out-of-sample robustness.
evidence: Distributional robustness of strategic equilibria is mature mathematical methodology outside video-game balancing.
limitation: Not a game-design parameter-selection or evaluator-population external-validity study.

work: XGuardian: Towards Generalized, Explainable and More Effective Server-side Anti-cheat in First-Person Shooter Games
method: USENIX Security 2026 system uses server-side pitch/yaw trajectory features and a GRU-CNN with SHAP-style explanation. Main CS2 data cover 3,069,216 aiming operations, 31,971 trajectories and 5,486 players; generalization is evaluated across CS2, CS:GO/HAWK data and Farlight84, with public datasets/artifacts.
evidence: Cross-game generalization, large-scale real-world validation, explainability and some adversarial robustness in FPS anti-cheat are directly occupied.
limitation: Temporal calibration/false-positive drift after patches or legitimate meta/style changes is not the core evaluation.

work: Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment in Serious Games: A Literature Review
area: DDA / systematic literature review / evaluation gaps
method: Reviews 75 recent serious-game DDA studies covering rule-based, player-model, physiological/emotional and machine-learning approaches. Finds growing use of adaptive systems but heterogeneous methods/evaluation metrics and substantial unresolved evaluation opportunities.
evidence: The DDA design space is broad and mature; another adaptation algorithm or isolated performance study is weak novelty.
limitation: The review does not identify a mature line of formal closed-loop stability analysis for simultaneous player-controller learning.

work: GameWorld: A Dynamic Benchmark for Generalist Agents in Interactive Game Environments
area: General game agents / interactive benchmark / evaluation protocol
method: GameWorld evaluates generalist agents on 34 browser games and 170 tasks using both low-level Computer-Use and semantic Generalist interfaces, state-verifiable progress/success metrics, a paused sandbox, and a real-time track. Full-paper audit shows interface choice can reverse relative model ordering; memory/context effects also differ by interface.
evidence: Large multi-game generalist-agent evaluation is current and state-verifiable; generic 'build a game-agent benchmark' is occupied.
limitation: The paper measures repeat-run robustness but does not formalize measurement invariance or ranking robustness across interface, latency regime, action budget, reset policy, scoring rule, memory harness and task mixture.

work: Software Testing Beyond Closed Worlds: Open-World Games as an Extreme Case
area: Open-world game testing / uncertainty / software engineering
method: FSE 2026 vision/research paper argues that open-world games violate closed-world testing assumptions through inexhaustible behavior spaces, nondeterminism, elusive behavioral boundaries and unstable test oracles. It calls for selective exploration under cost, repeated/long-running execution, behavior-oriented objectives, metrics beyond coverage/failure counts and longitudinal empirical validation.
evidence: The broad research agenda 'open-world testing needs new objectives, uncertainty-aware exploration and better oracles' is explicitly occupied.
limitation: A vision paper leaves many concrete problems open, but the same research line already produced boundary-oriented BBExplorer in ASE 2026, signaling fast author execution.

work: A Formal Framework for Critical-Mass Collapse in Online Multiplayer Games
area: Live-service viability / dynamical systems / population collapse
method: Defines a conditional Critical Mass Threshold Φ below which queue time, match quality or role balance makes a multiplayer game operationally non-viable under a fixed operational profile; models decline with threshold-sensitive hazards and emphasizes that Φ is really a projection of a higher-dimensional viability boundary depending on region, mode, roles, skill, party size, cross-play and time.
evidence: Critical-mass/viability collapse in online games now has an explicit mathematical framework.
limitation: Case studies are illustrative rather than formal validation. Heterogeneous subpopulations, multi-game competition, bots/AI substitution, UGC and private servers are explicit future-work directions.

work: Dynamic Balancing and Matchmaking in Competitive Live-Service Games
method: Working paper studies balancing and matchmaking as dynamically coupled operational levers under noisy game outcomes, emphasizing that estimation errors and intervention choices can interact nonlinearly.
evidence: Joint live-service balance+matchmaking optimization is already a current research object.
limitation: Working-paper status and specific model assumptions leave room for validation, but the broad synthesis is occupied.

work: Modeling Puzzle Difficulty via A* Search Behavior, Solution Paths, and Spatial Metrics
method: Studies A* search behavior, path and spatial features across Sokoban, Safari Rush Hour and Asteroid Escape.
evidence: Suggests shared latent patterns in how difficulty manifests across puzzle domains.
limitation: Difficulty estimation is adjacent rather than representation selection; early preprint.

work: Balanced Game Design
area: Operations research / game balance / equilibrium design
method: Formulates competitive video-game balancing as a two-stage optimization problem: the designer selects attributes that induce pairwise win rates, and players respond through a two-player zero-sum Nash equilibrium. Proves structural limits and NP-hardness, develops an approximate MIP, extends to alternative win-rate models and multi-scenario settings, and reports a real-game case study using AI-simulated gameplay.
evidence: Formal game-balance design, equilibrium response, optimization hardness, approximation and multi-scenario balance are already a strong 2026 operations-research program.
limitation: The accessible current version does not clearly establish robustness of the ACCEPTABLE BALANCE SET to evaluator-population or discovered-strategy-set shift; 'multi-scenario' makes even generic scenario-robustness a dangerous claim.

work: Turn-Based Combat Arena: A New Framework for Multiagent Training and Game Balancing
area: Multiagent simulation / game balancing / configurable benchmark
method: Introduces a high-throughput configurable turn-based combat environment for multiagent training/evaluation and automated unit balancing; several optimization approaches are reported to converge to comparable balance solutions.
evidence: Configurable simulation frameworks for automated combat balancing are current 2026 work.
limitation: Very recent preprint/first-in-series; current accessible evidence does not establish robustness to population/model shift. A fixed policy/evaluator can make a balance conclusion population-specific.

work: Matchmaking Strategies for Maximizing Player Engagement in Video Games
method: Management Science develops a dynamic matchmaking model with heterogeneous skill and loss aversion, considers bots/pay-to-win interventions, and evaluates the approach with real online-chess data.
evidence: Mathematical optimization of matchmaking quality, waiting/engagement and bot interventions is mature enough to close generic live-service matchmaking theses.
limitation: Does not estimate a critical-mass viability surface across fragmented live-service segments, but combines with current production systems to make that an incremental/high-race extension.

work: Enhancing Automated Video Game Regression Testing through Behavior-Driven Development and Imitation Learning
area: Automated game regression testing / BDD / RL / imitation learning
method: Combines natural-language BDD scenarios with imitation learning pretraining and RL fine-tuning to create adaptive automated regression tests; case study uses a Super Mario Bros clone in Godot and reports reduced test-development effort, improved coverage and detection of complex regressions.
evidence: BDD specifications + learned gameplay agents for regression testing are already a current Games-and-Software-Engineering contribution.
limitation: Single case-study game; reward design and RL compute remain limitations. It does not define cross-version semantic equivalence of behavior or exploit mechanisms.

work: NitroGen: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Gaming Agents
method: Vision-action foundation model trained on 40k hours across 1,000+ games; transfers to unseen games.
evidence: Cross-game zero-shot/few-shot transfer of PLAYER policies at large scale is now real, not hypothetical.
limitation: Acts in games; does not generate levels/instances or consume executable mechanics specifications.

work: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games
area: Causal reasoning / interactive games / agent diagnostics
method: ICML 2026 Oral benchmark with 14 SCM-governed interactive scenarios involving selection bias, measurement error and hidden confounding. Agents receive an experiment budget, design interventions and submit a final design plus explanation. Across 30 frontier LLM agents, the best reaches 68.0% survival versus analytical optima around 78–85%; only about 5–7% of sessions receive causal-reasoning credit. Behavioral failure analysis identifies component lock-in, bias and optimization drift.
evidence: Interactive intervention design, hidden causal mechanism discovery, and judge-independent failure-mode diagnostics in games are directly occupied.
limitation: The games model scientific discovery rather than PCG or game-rule transfer; SCM structure is hidden but fixed. It does not test complexity-separating mechanic conjunctions.

work: Mortar: Evolving Mechanics for Automatic Game Design
method: Uses QD + LLM to evolve mechanics; evaluates their contribution to skill-based player ordering and synthesizes complete games.
evidence: Mechanic generation plus skill-ordering evaluation is current 2026 prior art.
limitation: Still relies partly on user study and generated-game quality judgement; does not measure intrinsic computational demand or cross-rule transfer.

work: High Dimensional Procedural Content Generation
area: PCG / mechanics as coordinates / temporal-spatial representations
method: Formalizes HDPCG by promoting non-geometric gameplay dimensions to explicit coordinates. Direction-Space validates reachability in (x,y,z,layer) for mechanics such as gravity inversion/parallel worlds; Direction-Time uses time-expanded graphs for dynamic action/conflict semantics. Multiple algorithms and Unity case studies evaluate playability, robustness, structure, style and efficiency.
evidence: Mechanics-aware, temporal and higher-dimensional PCG representations are already an explicit FDG 2026 framework rather than an unoccupied direction.
limitation: The paper demonstrates selected mechanic dimensions rather than automatic representation selection, theorem-derived complexity activation or transfer laws across puzzle families.

work: Constraint-Based Four-Dimensional Spacetime Blending of Learned Game Mechanics Along Orthogonal Planes
area: Mechanic blending / learned mechanics / constraint PCG
method: Learns tile-based mechanics from example playthroughs as changes in tile configurations, blends mechanics from separate 2D games along orthogonal planes to form a 3D game, and generates a solution jointly with the level using temporal constraints in a conceptual 4D spacetime representation.
evidence: Learned cross-game mechanic blending with explicit compositional geometry and guaranteed-completion constraints is directly published in FDG 2026.
limitation: The work targets a specific orthogonal-plane blending construction rather than algebra-preserving learned generators or frozen transfer to unseen executable dynamics.

work: PACE: Parameter Change for Unsupervised Environment Design
method: Values environments by the magnitude of policy-parameter change induced by training, using a first-order approximation to realized learning progress rather than regret/value-error/Monte-Carlo proxies. Reports improved OOD IQM and optimality-gap results on MiniGrid and Craftax.
evidence: Environment usefulness/learning-progress estimation is already being attacked directly with agent-update signals in 2026 UED.
limitation: Not game-mechanic theorem structure or causal testing; environment value is still policy-dependent and not a failure-attribution mechanism.

work: A Tractability Gap Beyond Nim-Sums: It's Hard to Tell Whether a Bunch of Superstars Are Losers
method: Shows that disjunctive sums of simple tepid canonical game components (superstars) are NP-hard to solve, extending a long line where sums of individually tractable games can become PSPACE/NP-hard.
evidence: The broad principle 'combining simple/tractable game components can create computational intractability' is already established beyond video-game mechanics.
limitation: Composition is algebraic/disjunctive sum, not semantic mechanic conjunction on a matched level; no finite empirical solver-activation study.

work: Where Does Balance Break? Boundary Discovery for Game Balance Testing under a Finite Simulation Budget
area: Game balance regression / boundary discovery / simulation budget
method: ASE 2026 research paper formulates balance regression testing as discovering the boundary between balanced and unbalanced regions in a stochastic parameter space under a finite simulation budget. BBExplorer combines multi-directional candidates, two-stage budget-aware screening and adaptive step-size refinement; evaluation covers two games and reports robustness to unseen random seeds/thresholds.
evidence: The generic object 'find a game-balance boundary efficiently under a finite simulation budget' is directly occupied.
limitation: Accessible current evidence does not establish robustness to changes in evaluator/player populations or an expanding strategic response set; the reported robustness is to stochastic seeds and threshold settings.

work: Representations for the Procedural Content Generation of Puzzle Game Instances: A Systematic Literature Review
method: SLR: 931 records screened for 2020–2025, 111 studies included; classifies logical vs physical representations.
evidence: Explicitly concludes a significant gap in representation selection; notes search-space topology induced by logical representation has not been prioritized.
limitation: Review itself does not solve selection; it maps the gap. Same authors are already pursuing follow-up experiments.

work: MirrorCraft: Paired Evaluation under Hidden Rule Changes in Minecraft
method: Pairs Vanilla and Mirror worlds while matching terrain, spawn, resources, objective, interface and action budget; only rules change.
evidence: Paired controlled game-rule interventions are established methodology.
limitation: Evaluates agent progress under bundled rule suites rather than decomposing true search cost vs model-learning adequacy.

work: Control-oriented system identification: Classical, learning, and physics-informed approaches
method: Survey argues identification should preserve downstream control-relevant properties rather than minimize prediction error; highlights guarantees and sample complexity.
evidence: The broader control field already treats model adequacy as downstream-task relative.
limitation: Not about discrete game mechanics, matched interventions, or planner/model burden separation.

work: Multiverse Mechanica: A Testbed for Learning Game Mechanics via Counterfactual Worlds
area: Game world models / causal mechanic learning
method: Formalizes mechanics as causal counterfactual constraints and emits paired worlds plus per-mechanic causal graphs for learning/evaluation.
evidence: Mechanic-level counterfactual world-model learning is now directly occupied in games.
limitation: Targets causal consistency of generated frames and single-impact frames, not samples-to-planning-adequacy or true-game search burden.

work: When a Verified World Model Still Loses: Play-Adequacy vs Prediction-Accuracy in LLM-Synthesized Code World Models
method: Shows sampled transition/state accuracy can be near perfect while a rare omitted rule causes systematic play loss; advocates search-distribution or play adequacy.
evidence: Raw prediction accuracy is invalid as G078-R's model-learning endpoint; rare pivotal rules are already demonstrated.
limitation: Single/few failure constructions; does not map mechanic interventions to both planning burden and sample-to-adequacy burden.

work: Automated planning instance generation with neuro-symbolic AI
method: Generates valid, diverse and difficult planning problems using a neuro-symbolic generative model and deep RL.
evidence: Automatic valid hard-instance generation in planning is current prior art.
limitation: Targets generic difficulty and validity, not holding one learned-model/planning burden fixed while separating the other.

work: Mortar: Evolving Mechanics for Automatic Game Design
method: Evolves game mechanics with QD and evaluates mechanic contribution through skill-based ordering across generated games.
evidence: Mechanic contribution/attribution and mechanic evolution are occupied.
limitation: Does not attribute mechanic effects separately to planning-search burden and planning-adequate model-learning burden.

work: Refploit: Facilitating Exploit Construction via Code-Agent Trajectory Repair
method: Uses differential execution to decompose failed exploit trajectories into satisfied, missing and misleading subtasks, then derives preservation/repair constraints and iteratively repairs the trajectory.
evidence: Semantic trajectory repair and differential exploit validation are already active in software engineering.
limitation: Targets code-agent vulnerability reproduction, not interactive gameplay policies or causal exploit equivalence across stochastic/dynamic builds.

work: Finding Shortest Walks in Kuru Kuru Kururin
method: Mechanic-wise complexity analysis plus faithful game recreation and search experiments.
evidence: Directly bridges theoretical mechanic complexity and practical search difficulty in a commercial game.
limitation: Does not use a matched factorial intervention where individually tractable mechanic families are switched on/off on the same finite instance.

work: EMemBench: Interactive Benchmarking of Episodic Memory for VLM Agents
method: Programmatically generates verifiable trajectory-grounded questions across 15 text games and visual settings; covers recall, induction, temporal, spatial, logical and adversarial memory.
evidence: Game-based capability-specific dynamic benchmarking is rapidly maturing.
limitation: Memory-agent evaluation, not game-level marginal demand for memory.

work: Causal Reinforcement Learning for Complex Card Games: A Magic The Gathering Benchmark
area: Causal RL / transfer / policy auditability / games
method: Introduces MTG-Causal-RL with a 3,077-D partial observation, 478 masked actions, five Standard archetypes, three rewards and a hand-designed SCM. Each episode exposes causal variables, predicted intervention effects and per-factor credit traces. Evaluation includes paired-seed PPO/causal baselines, leave-one-archetype-out transfer, calibration curves and factor credit shares.
evidence: SCM-grounded factor-level credit attribution plus held-out game-strategy transfer and policy auditability already coexist in a 2026 game benchmark.
limitation: SCM is hand-designed; only five archetypes and 56 cards; opponents are fixed; headline learned-agent results use a small seed count and causal augmentation does not uniformly improve win rate.

work: Population-dependent agent performance in non-transitive games: a multi-agent rock–paper–scissors benchmark
method: Evaluates 54 agents from 18 archetypes and shows rankings change with opponent roster; reports Spearman rank correlation about 0.83 between two rosters and a change in the top-ranked method.
evidence: Direct 2026 evidence that rank order itself is population-dependent in a game benchmark; generic roster-induced rank reversal/instability is occupied.
limitation: Non-transitive agent performance, not automatic game design and not mechanic contribution attribution.

work: GameRule: a multi-agent architecture for game behavior specification
area: Game rule specification / DSL / multi-agent architecture
method: Introduces a rule-based DSL with per-actor when-do rules, CRUD state operations, deterministic central scheduling and a Unity code-generation backend.
evidence: Explicit executable rule/behavior specification for games remains an active fast-moving systems frontier; broad claims around new game-rule DSLs or executable behavior specification are high race.
limitation: Does not address cross-game zero-shot learned designers, complexity-critical mechanic activation, or representation-selection laws.

work: Evaluating SAT Solver Metrics as Predictors of Human-Perceived Nonogram Difficulty
method: Encodes 10×10 Nonograms in SAT; evaluates MiniSat decisions, propagations and conflicts. From 1,000 uniquely solvable puzzles, selects six and runs a 67-participant / 201-attempt user study. Puzzle-level Spearman correlations with reported difficulty are decisions −0.257, propagations −0.257 and conflicts 0.000, all nonsignificant; expertise moderates the relationship.
evidence: Solver effort cannot automatically be interpreted as human-perceived difficulty; human and computational difficulty can decouple strongly.
limitation: Small six-puzzle human sample and one puzzle family; does not study mechanic interventions or complexity-class interactions.

work: Modeling Puzzle Difficulty via A* Search Behavior, Solution Paths, and Spatial Metrics
method: Full-text author manuscript uses six datasets across Sokoban, Safari Rush Hour and Asteroid Escape. It extracts A*-search/solution/spatial features, tests Spearman association with expert/user difficulty, clustering consistency and intra-/inter-game generalization. Sliding-puzzle families transfer more consistently; cross-domain pairs involving Sokoban are notably less stable.
evidence: Cross-dataset and cross-puzzle generalization of solver-derived difficulty features is already an explicit 2026 research question.
limitation: Difficulty labels mix expert ratings, completion behavior and user perception; rules are fixed within each puzzle family. It does not identify causal rule/mechanic interventions or complexity-separating conjunctions.

work: Adapting a content orchestrator across game genres: From top-down adventure to 2D platformer
area: Cross-genre PCG / content orchestration / player adaptation
method: Adapts the existing Overlord content orchestrator from a top-down adventure game to a 2D platformer. Core level/rule/narrative orchestration and player profiling are retained with mostly small parameter/implementation changes; only the low-level room generator needs substantial modification. Mixed-methods evaluation uses 168 questionnaire responses from 103 players plus think-aloud/interviews with 11 participants.
evidence: Cross-genre reuse of an existing procedural content orchestrator is now directly demonstrated in 2026, including adaptive content and human evaluation.
limitation: The two genres share substantial structure (room exploration, combat, quests, lock-key progression); authors explicitly say radically different genres may require redesign. This is adaptation, not frozen zero-shot transfer.

work: AI Native Games: A Survey and Roadmap
method: Defines AI-native games via counterfactual dependence of the core loop on runtime generative AI; reviews 53 artifacts and identifies open design areas.
evidence: Runtime GenAI-as-mechanic is becoming a distinct field with a fresh taxonomy.
limitation: Most research questions involve semantic openness, human experience, controllability, evaluation and safety; poor fit for no-human MSc constraints.

work: Computational Complexity and Integer Programming Formulation of the Oredango Puzzle
area: Puzzle complexity / exact optimization / empirical solving
method: Proves NP- and ASP-completeness, formulates a 0-1 integer program, and reports numerical results on real Oredango instances from Nikoli and PuzzleSquare JP.
evidence: The combination 'puzzle complexity theorem + solver formulation + numerical experiments on real finite instances' is explicitly occupied in 2026.
limitation: Does not perform matched mechanic interventions, factorial ablations, cross-distribution finite activation, or solver-robust interaction estimation.

work: Constructing Maximally Difficult Sliding-Block Puzzles Using State Space Analysis
method: Bachelor thesis listed in LIACS 2025–2026 repository studying difficult sliding-block puzzles via state-space analysis.
evidence: Shows recent empirical interest in sliding-block state-space difficulty and hard-instance construction.
limitation: Grey literature / bachelor thesis; does not appear to target the theorem-matched 1×1→1×2 boundary.

work: Which Structural Constraints Are Learnable? A Regime Map for a Minecraft Voxel Generator
method: FDG 2026 diagnostic study fixes a VQ-VAE + autoregressive Transformer voxel pipeline and measures 14 structural properties under conditioning. Nine are controllable, four approachable and one unresponsive; a composite effective-signal × min(CV,1) predictor correlates with controllability at Spearman ρ=0.879 (permutation p=0.002, n=10 emergent properties). Authors explicitly warn this is one-pipeline association, not a universal predictor.
evidence: Predicting whether structural PCG constraints are learnable/controllable and diagnosing frequency-floor vs representation-ceiling patterns is already a direct 2026 PCG object.
limitation: Single Minecraft voxel pipeline; bottleneck labels are heuristic rather than causally identified; predictor has not been externally validated across architectures/datasets/domains.

work: ClassicLogic: A Knowledge-Driven Benchmark of Classic Puzzle Games for Evaluating Compositional Generalization
method: Procedurally generates Sudoku, KenKen, Kakuro and Futoshiki with hierarchical strategy knowledge; evaluates cross-game zero-shot entity/relational transfer and procedural composition.
evidence: Cross-puzzle compositional reasoning benchmarks are already arriving in 2026.
limitation: Focuses reasoning agents and strategy composition, not representation effects on PCG search or frozen designer transfer.

work: Reasoning Core: A Scalable Procedural Data Generation Suite for Symbolic Pre-training and Post-Training
method: Procedurally samples verifiable symbolic tasks including randomized PDDL domains, first-order logic, grammars and causal models with continuous difficulty and external solvers.
evidence: Formal-domain procedural generation with broad distributional coverage is rapidly becoming benchmark infrastructure.
limitation: Generates reasoning data/tasks, not game levels via a transferred learned designer.

work: Procedural Content Metageneration via Program Search and Continual Abstraction Discovery
method: Full-text reread: evolves complete Python generator programs for Sokoban, Zelda, Dangerous Dave and Lode Runner. Main experiment is CAD × fixed Expert API (2×2), 160 completed 50-generation runs; each candidate is executed 30 times and scored on validity, benchmark quality and diversity. CAD improves mean final best fitness in all eight domain/API comparisons; exact sign test p=0.008.
evidence: Generator-space evolutionary program search and search-time abstraction discovery across multiple games are already active 2026 contributions; generic 'generator of generators' and adaptive vocabulary claims are occupied.
limitation: Each run still adapts inside one target domain. The authors explicitly list cross-run library transfer as future work and do not test one frozen learned designer/spec transferred to unseen executable dynamics.

work: Tape: A Cellular Automata Benchmark for Evaluating Rule-Shift Generalization in Reinforcement Learning
method: Keeps observation/action spaces fixed while transition rules change; compares model-free, learned-world-model planning and meta-RL under held-out rule shifts.
evidence: Rule-shift generalization itself is now explicitly benchmarked on the acting-agent side.
limitation: Agent/world-model evaluation, not procedural designer transfer or target-level generation.

work: Simulation to Rules: A Dual-VLM Framework for Formal Visual Planning
method: Learns to infer formal planning descriptions and plans from visual simulations and evaluates unseen rule variants with iterative refinement.
evidence: Formal-rule generalization and unseen-rule evaluation are active in 2026.
limitation: Planner/rule-induction setting rather than procedural instance designer; iterative refinement also differs from frozen zero-target generation.

work: Multiverse: Language-Conditioned Multi-Game Level Blending via Shared Representation
method: Conditional VQ-VAE learns a shared text-level latent space across four game domains and performs zero-shot generation from unseen composite text prompts plus cross-game latent interpolation.
evidence: Single-model multi-game generation and zero-shot compositional prompts are explicitly established in 2026.
limitation: The game domains themselves are present during training; 'zero-shot' refers to unseen composite instructions, not an unseen executable game dynamics system.

work: What Game Developers Actually Want from Procedural Level Generation Tools
method: Empirically examines developer needs/preferences for procedural level-generation tooling.
evidence: Confirms practical PCG evaluation/control concerns but shifts toward HCI/tool adoption.
limitation: Not a low-compute formal thesis object.

work: Regular Games — an Automata-Based General Game Playing Language
method: Defines a universal automata-based language for finite turn-based imperfect-information games and reports fast forward models relative to other GGP systems.
evidence: New lightweight formal infrastructure for cross-game experimental research.
limitation: Infrastructure/language, not a thesis gap itself.

work: Mortar: Evolving Mechanics for Automatic Game Design
method: Evolves code-level mechanics with QD+LLM; evaluates complete games by skill-based ordering over a fixed pool of five agents and introduces CITS, a search-constrained Shapley-style mechanic contribution score.
evidence: Closest direct anchor for G049: mechanic quality is explicitly attributed through an evaluator population.
limitation: Uses one fixed agent pool; does not systematically test whether mechanic rankings/contributions persist across independent evaluator populations or agent families.

work: Best Agent Identification for General Game Playing
method: Frames best-agent identification over many games as multiple best-arm identification problems and substantially reduces simple regret under limited trials.
evidence: Efficient best-agent identification is a current solved/active research object.
limitation: Does not explain semantic reasons why one agent fits a game.

work: Beyond Fixed Tasks: Unsupervised Environment Design for Task-Level Pairs
method: AAAI 2026 full-paper line: ATLAS extends UED from fixed tasks to joint autocurricula over reward-machine task specifications and MiniGrid levels, explicitly generating solvable yet challenging task-level pairs. Structure-aware mutations over both task and level improve convergence over random pairing.
evidence: Task–environment co-design, solvability-aware curriculum generation, and joint mutation of specifications and levels are occupied UED contributions.
limitation: Does not use game-complexity mechanic theorems or attribute failures to particular rule interactions.

work: From Gameplay Traces to Game Mechanics: Causal Induction with Large Language Models
method: Infers SCMs and VGDL rules from gameplay traces; SCM-first generation improves logical consistency/fidelity over direct rule generation.
evidence: Game-specific causal induction from traces is now directly occupied.
limitation: Does not estimate causal treatment effects of controlled mechanics on players/content.

work: Quality-Diversity Algorithms under Variable Constraints Competition (QDA-VC)
method: AIIDE 2026 competition evaluates QD methods under changing/add-remove constraints across puzzles, Lode Runner and optimization domains.
evidence: Variable constraint handling is an active benchmark frontier now.
limitation: Competition does not causally diagnose why a constraint is unresponsive.

work: Evolutionary Wave Function Collapse
method: Treats WFC inputs as an evolvable genotype-to-phenotype mapping and evaluates Maze and Zelda, finding stronger results when objectives align with local structure than global constraints.
evidence: Generator performance depends on how representation/operator locality matches objective structure; this relationship is actively studied.
limitation: Not a controlled equivalent-encoding study and no held-out representation-selection model.

work: MOSAIC: Adversarial Co-evolution of Specialist Heuristics and Problem Instances for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design
method: Co-evolves discriminative combinatorial instances and specialist heuristics in an instance-feature QD archive; maps regions where heuristics win.
evidence: Feature-conditioned hard-instance generation and algorithm specialization are very active.
limitation: General combinatorial optimization and LLM-assisted heuristic design; not theorem-linked game-mechanic causal intervention.

work: Generative Executable Algorithm Knowledge Graphs (GEAKG)
method: Represents executable algorithm operators and learned composition patterns in a transferable knowledge graph; reports zero-shot transfer from TSP to scheduling/assignment under a shared solution representation.
evidence: Zero-shot transfer of procedural algorithmic know-how across optimization domains is now explicit.
limitation: Algorithm design/solver procedures, not game-content designers; transfer relies on shared representation protocol and domain ontologies.

work: Representing and Generating Levels Over Time through Playtrace Reconstructive Partitioning
method: Full-text reread: defines the cake representation as a k×n×m Markovian sequence of game-state slices with persistent temporal entities, then introduces PRP, a time-aware reconstructive partitioning generator. Sokoban evaluation uses 12 human-authored 7×7 source levels and compares against PoD, Sturgeon-MKIII, Sturgeon-ST, two PCGRL settings, and an LSTM baseline. PRP reaches 100% playability and competitive diversity; case studies apply the same base algorithm to OvercookedAI and a new SkeleWalker domain.
evidence: Dynamic temporal level representation plus domain-agnostic generation is already a full FDG 2026 contribution, including multi-domain case studies.
limitation: The authors explicitly note domain-specific pre/post-processing, potentially lossy conversion, non-identical baseline corpora, and lack of broad statistical comparison. They do NOT isolate the causal effect of representation from generator/search algorithm, and robust evaluation is primarily Sokoban.

work: Carrying is Hard: Exploring the Gap between Hardness for NP and PSPACE for the Hanano and Jelly no Puzzles
method: Compares complexity under restrictions for two related puzzles and identifies block carrying as a likely mechanism sustaining PSPACE-hardness.
evidence: Recent puzzle theory continues isolating mechanics responsible for complexity-class differences.
limitation: Theoretical classification only; no empirical finite-instance solver study.

work: Finding Shortest Walks in Kuru Kuru Kururin
method: Full-text reread: combines formal complexity analysis with a faithful ~4k-line C# recreation and custom A*-based KuruBot. Current experiments solve original levels under damageless/intended/unrestricted-physics settings; the paper does NOT yet benchmark a controlled level suite isolating diagonal movement, springs and moving objects one-by-one.
evidence: The broad contribution 'connect computational game complexity to practical solver behavior in a commercial game' is occupied. It also demonstrates that physics/mechanic settings can be changed in practical solver experiments.
limitation: Conclusion explicitly proposes future work to generate levels focused on individual mechanics (no diagonal moves, diagonal moves, springs, moving objects), benchmark KuruBot, and compare those results with the complexity analysis. It still does not study a conjunction whose every strict subset is tractable nor a matched Boolean-lattice interaction contrast.

work: Learning Bayesian Game Families, with Application to Mechanism Design
method: Learn game-family models across mechanism/environment parameters; supports parameter search/extrapolation.
evidence: Game-family modeling for design-space exploration is advancing beyond one fixed game.
limitation: Mechanism-design focus; not game-mechanic capability fingerprints.

work: Using Effective State Representations and Search to Identify Interesting Safari Rush Hour Puzzle Instances
method: Full-preprint reread: proposes a cluster/enumeration representation for Safari Rush Hour, compares two traversal strategies (systematic per-board IDA*+TT vs retrograde analysis over clusters) and compares the proposed encoding against two board representations. Roughly 28-hour searches show the enumeration representation is more efficient than a naive list-of-pieces encoding, and retrograde analysis finds longer-solution instances faster.
evidence: A direct 2026 representation × search study now exists in the exact puzzle-PCG community that identified representation selection as a gap.
limitation: Single primary domain and representation/search are not fully orthogonal: the cluster representation is designed to enable retrograde exploration. It does not provide semantic-matched representation interventions or a validated cross-family selection law.

work: Stochastic Safe Action Model Learning
method: Gives polynomial time/sample complexity for a bounded-support stochastic planning-model class and guarantees approximate completeness from offline trajectories.
evidence: Planning-adequate learned models with explicit sample guarantees remain an active 2026 planning line.
limitation: No game-mechanic counterfactual decomposition and no comparison with true-engine solver burden.

work: Multiverse Mechanica: A Testbed for Learning Game Mechanics via Counterfactual Worlds
method: Full-paper audit: formalizes a mechanic as causal structure plus counterfactual constraints and generates 'consistent contrasts' from parallel game worlds with shared initial conditions/random seed so non-target context remains matched. Proof-of-concept mechanics include shield/weapon and spell/element-style interactions; the learning experiment fine-tunes an image-generation model on impact-frame counterfactuals with seed-consistency and structural-alignment losses.
evidence: Causal/counterfactual game-mechanic signatures, matched mechanic worlds, and causal consistency are already an ICLR 2026 research contribution.
limitation: Current testbed is simplified and proof-of-concept; it models single impact frames rather than complete temporal rollouts. Authors identify richer 3D/continuous/temporal mechanics and causal-consistency metrics across entire rollouts as future work.

work: Distilling Game Code World Model Generation into Lightweight Large Language Models
method: Introduces a 30-game dataset, structural/property-based checks and execution-based trajectory verification, then post-trains a 3B model with SFT+RLVR for GameCWM generation.
evidence: Game-model verification using properties and trajectory matching is directly active in 2026; semantic adherence itself is not an empty space.
limitation: Its verification is based on predefined properties and sparse/lightweight trajectories; it does not search over game content to construct minimal behavioral counterexamples or bounded equivalence certificates.

work: From Gameplay Traces to Game Mechanics: Causal Induction with Large Language Models
method: Reverse-engineers VGDL rules from short gameplay traces using direct LLM synthesis or an SCM-mediated pipeline across representative GVGAI games.
evidence: Learning executable/structured game mechanics from observations is a current 2026 research line.
limitation: Authors note confusion between mechanically similar games when traces fail to expose distinguishing transitions; current parsability/code-similarity/judge metrics do not adequately measure causal fidelity; only one observation set per game is used.

work: State-based Parameter Evolving with Lightweight Optimization for Graph Adaptation to Evolving Shifts
method: Uses a test-time evolving state controller and lightweight generated adapters for sequential graph domain shifts, with replay-free adaptation and stability regularization.
evidence: Selective/lightweight adaptation to evolving graph shifts is now an active WWW 2026 topic.
limitation: Does not explicitly decompose observed drift into feature/topology/label/relation sources before choosing what model component to adapt.

work: Carrying is Hard: Exploring the Gap between Hardness for NP and PSPACE for the Hanano and Jelly no Puzzles
method: Full-text reread: one-color Hanano remains PSPACE-complete without movable gray blocks; width-1 movable blocks make Hanano NP-complete; for every constant k, Hanano and Jelly with at most k movable blocks are in P. Authors posit simulated carrying as the mechanism behind the NP→PSPACE gap rather than prove a generic necessary/sufficient carrying dichotomy.
evidence: The restriction lattice and carrying hypothesis are directly owned by the theory authors; finite empirical activation is the only remaining nearby object.
limitation: No finite-instance solver study is present. However, same-geometry 'carrying off/on' intervention is not given by the theorem and the paper's future work explicitly seeks a more general framework for carrying/sliding games.

work: DRIFT: A Benchmark for Task-Free Continual Graph Learning with Continuous Distribution Shifts
method: Introduces task-free graph streams with hard, blurry and continuous Gaussian distribution shifts and shows large degradation of existing continual graph methods without task boundaries.
evidence: The earlier external backup premise 'task-free graph continual learning under continuous drift' is directly occupied.
limitation: Does not attribute which source of graph drift (features/topology/labels/relations) caused failure or adapt only the implicated component.

work: AI-Native Games: A Survey and Roadmap
method: Defines AI-native core-loop dependence; analyzes 53 artifacts; identifies semantic adjudication, multi-agent simulation and generative construction as underrepresented; emphasizes mechanical invariants.
evidence: Mechanical invariants under runtime semantic openness are a genuine new frontier.
limitation: Roadmap-visible gap creates high race risk; LLM safety/testing/formal validation are major adjacent literatures.

work: Mind-Studio: Executable World Models with Lookahead Evaluation for Partially Observable Games
method: Synthesizes pygame-style world models from object-centric trajectories and evaluates them with K-step lookahead fidelity against real Atari rollouts.
evidence: Multi-step behavioral fidelity evaluation of executable game world models is already current work.
limitation: Evaluation starts from observed snapshots/branches and does not synthesize game content or minimal counterexamples between rule hypotheses.

work: Code World Models for General Game Playing
area: General game playing / learned executable models
method: Learns executable Python world models from natural-language rules/traces and uses them with planning/MCTS across multiple games.
evidence: Executable learned game models and multi-game transfer are now active current-frontier research.
limitation: Does not directly study content-realizable equivalence or counterfactual rule interrogation.

work: NitroGen: A Foundation Agent for Generalist Game Playing
method: Large multi-game training corpus and generalist game agent; targets zero-shot/off-the-shelf and transfer across many games.
evidence: Generalist game-playing is becoming a scale/foundation-model race.
limitation: High compute and not focused on formal rule changes or game design.

work: Taming the Search Space: Solving and Generating Hitori and Binairo Puzzles
method: Generates benchmark instances and compares optimized backtracking and SAT solving across puzzle sizes, measuring runtime, search nodes and branching behavior.
evidence: Modern puzzle research already expects generated benchmarks, multiple solver paradigms and search-effort instrumentation.
limitation: No mechanic intervention or complexity-class interaction treatment.

work: Multi-task Procedural Content Generation with Reinforcement Learning
method: Peer-reviewed OA article trains language-conditioned PCGRL for Mario-style surface-feature control with a DeBERTa instruction encoder and regression/contrastive/hybrid objectives. Evaluation explicitly includes single-task, additive, compositional, paraphrased and zero-shot/extrapolative instruction regimes; complex or conflicting constraints remain the weak regime.
evidence: Instruction-conditioned and compositional/OOD control in PCGRL is directly being benchmarked in 2026.
limitation: The target remains one known game/dynamics family; the generator is not frozen and transferred spec-only to unseen executable transition semantics.

work: VIPCGRL: Visual Instruction-based Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning
method: Uses aligned textual/visual level-sketch representations to guide RL-based generation and improve human-aligned controllability.
evidence: Representation/control innovation in PCGRL is moving rapidly into multimodal/shared semantic spaces.
limitation: Not equivalent-representation causal science and not held-out dynamics transfer.

work: Five Emerging Research Opportunities for Deep Learning in Video Games
method: Highlights emerging opportunities including LLM agents, neural cellular automata for PCG, deep surrogate modeling, self-supervised game-state representations and interactive worlds.
evidence: Independent recent agenda supports surrogate modeling and NCA as live game-AI directions.
limitation: Agenda/opinion; does not establish a specific unoccupied research question.

work: Learning Local Constraints for Reinforcement-Learned Content Generators
method: Combines learned/local WFC-style constraints with reinforcement-learned content generators and studies how local structural constraints affect generation; notes potential transfer implications.
evidence: Representation/local-constraint coupling with PCGRL is an active 2026 frontier.
limitation: Does not provide canonical equivalent representations with semantic-matched edits or cross-family representation-selection boundaries.

work: High Dimensional Procedural Content Generation
method: Represents mechanics as additional dimensions such as layer/time and evaluates procedural generation over expanded state spaces; explicitly discusses composition of multiple dimensions as future work.
evidence: Single-axis high-dimensional mechanic representations and their generation are already published.
limitation: Axes are evaluated separately; multi-mechanic joint composition, scaling and interaction are left open, but this is explicit author future work and therefore high race risk.

work: Evolving Programmatic Skill Networks
method: Maintains an evolving graph of executable symbolic skills with trace-based credit assignment, stabilization and refactoring; demonstrates reuse/generalization in MineDojo and Crafter.
evidence: Programmatic skill libraries, compositional reuse and continual reorganization are rapidly advancing outside compact formal-game settings.
limitation: Does not focus on cross-rule formal invariance or predicting transferability from rule structure.

work: Learning Abstractions for Hierarchical Planning in Program-Synthesis Agents
method: TheoryCoder-2 learns PDDL abstractions/skills and reuses them across VGDL games, BabyAI and MiniHack; demonstrates zero-shot abstraction reuse with no domain adaptation for several tasks.
evidence: Learning and reusing symbolic/programmatic abstractions across game-like domains is now directly demonstrated.
limitation: Does not systematically characterize formal rule-structural conditions predicting positive versus negative concept transfer, but occupies the broad G031 thesis question.

work: Reward-Adaptive Iterative Discovery: A Case Study on Automated Game Testing for NHL26
method: EA trains iterative RL agents to discover multiple diverse goalie exploits. The paper explicitly states that after a behavior update, absence of the exploit in a rerun or failure of the old policy is not enough to prove the exploit was fixed because policies overfit exact dynamics.
evidence: Diverse exploit discovery is occupied, while reliable cross-version exploit-fix verification remains an explicit industrial limitation.
limitation: Still requires humans to determine whether strategies are true exploits and to validate fixes; proprietary NHL setting limits reusable benchmark evidence.

work: Knowledge Graph-enhanced Large Language Model for Incremental Game PlayTesting
area: Game testing / knowledge graphs / incremental updates
method: Current journal audit: KLPEG maintains a knowledge graph of game elements, task dependencies and causal relationships across versions; an LLM parses update logs, uses multi-hop KG reasoning to identify impacted functionality, and generates targeted incremental playtests. Evaluated on Overcooked and Minecraft.
evidence: Cross-version structured knowledge accumulation, impact localization and update-tailored game testing are directly occupied.
limitation: The framework depends on update-log interpretation and does not define semantic equivalence of a behavior/exploit when concrete traces or implementations change.

work: Seduced by the Narrative: Assessing Rule Adherence in Semi-Open Textual Games (CoC-Seduce)
method: Builds an adversarial benchmark on tabletop RPG mechanics with explicit rules and natural-language interaction; 5,376 samples, multiple adversarial generators and 20 adjudicator models; finds rule-adjudication robustness remains difficult.
evidence: Directly occupies the idea of benchmarking LLM semantic game adjudication/rule adherence under adversarial natural-language play.
limitation: May not cover persistent mechanical invariants/state transitions or repair architectures across model versions, but the core evaluation object is very close.

work: Finite Automata Extraction: Low-data World Model Learning as Programs from Gameplay Video
method: Learns symbolic/programmatic game dynamics from very little gameplay video in Pac-Man/River Raid.
evidence: Direct current evidence that low-data game-rule/world-model extraction is active.
limitation: Does not by itself resolve observational identifiability under passive support.

work: Diffploit: Facilitating Cross-Version Exploit Migration for Open Source Library Vulnerabilities
method: Adapts failing exploits across Java library versions using behavioral discrepancies, code diffs and iterative LLM-guided repair; reports 84.2% migration over 689 tasks.
evidence: Cross-version exploit migration is a mature, directly analogous software-engineering problem by 2026.
limitation: Code/API exploit setting differs from interactive game exploits with long-horizon state/action semantics and often no useful source-level diff.

work: Synergizing Code Coverage and Gameplay Intent: Coverage-Aware Game Playtesting with LLM-Guided RL
method: Journal-version audit: SMART interprets AST differences with an LLM, decomposes update intent into ordered gameplay subgoals, maps those subgoals to modified-code anchors, and trains RL agents with a hybrid functional+coverage reward. Evaluation spans Overcooked, Minecraft and MineDojo; reported modified-branch coverage reaches up to 98% in structured environments and 72% in MineDojo while task completion remains 79–98%.
evidence: Update-aware automated game testing that connects code diffs, semantic gameplay intent, RL exploration, and structural coverage is directly occupied.
limitation: It does not prove cross-version behavioral equivalence, exploit-mechanism persistence, or minimal causal counterexamples; LLM-extracted intent and reward construction remain framework components rather than formal guarantees.

work: Backdoors to satisfaction continued
method: Reviews current parameterized-complexity results for backdoor size, depth and treewidth into polynomial-time SAT classes.
evidence: Confirms backdoor/tractability-distance theory is mature and still active in 2026.
limitation: Review is SAT-focused; does not occupy a game-specific theorem if one exists.

work: CA2: Code-Aware Agent for Automated Game Testing
method: Uses code/call-stack context to guide automated agents toward target functions in games.
evidence: Modern game testers increasingly incorporate implementation structure rather than only black-box gameplay.
limitation: Code access assumptions differ from semantic mechanic testing.

work: Adversarial Instance Generation and Robust Training for Neural Combinatorial Optimization with Multiple Objectives
method: Generates hard/adversarial combinatorial instances against learned solvers and uses them for robust training.
evidence: Hard-instance generators can overfit a solver and adversarial generation is established.
limitation: Neural CO and multiobjective optimization, not mechanic-ablation interaction in games.

work: Embedded Mechanics Generation
method: Generates mechanics, reconstructs levels, and creates enemies supporting newly generated mechanics; compares RL and A*-style agents and proposes DIA.
evidence: Joint mechanic-level-enemy generation/evaluation is already being pursued.
limitation: Doctoral/ongoing line; designer-intent validation and evaluation remain challenging.

work: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
method: Evaluates seven UI agents over more than 10,000 runs on configurable app variants and finds that success can change dramatically across semantically related environment versions.
evidence: Reliability under environment variation is already directly studied for interactive agents.
limitation: Variation concerns app appearance/content rather than game action-interface/latency/metric protocol and model ranking invariance.

work: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
method: Shows that task setup and reward/evaluator design can substantially distort agent benchmark results and proposes the Agentic Benchmark Checklist. Applying the checklist can materially change measured performance.
evidence: Benchmark validity, evaluator confounding and rigorous agent measurement are already an explicit research line.
limitation: Not game-specific and does not study rank invariance across game interaction protocols.

work: Integrating Reinforcement Learning, Action Model Learning, and Numeric Planning for Tackling Complex Tasks
method: Compares learned numeric domain models + planning with alternative learning approaches in Minecraft tasks, including offline and online model acquisition.
evidence: Game-adjacent action-model learning for planning is already empirically studied.
limitation: Does not intervene on individual mechanics or decompose planning-search versus model-acquisition burden.

work: Different Forms of Imbalance in Strongly Playable Discrete Games I: Two-Player RPS Games
method: Develops formal definitions of imbalance and playability for strongly playable discrete two-player games and relates them to dominated strategies; shows balance is mathematically richer than equal empirical win rates.
evidence: Formalizing game balance metrics themselves is an active mathematical research line.
limitation: Abstract RPS-like setting rather than live-service parameter-space robustness or player-population shift.

work: A Study on a Reinforcement Learning-based Player-Adaptive Dynamic Game Difficulty Adjustment System
method: Uses a Player Agent and Balancing Agent in a physics-based game. The paper explicitly states that simultaneous learning creates non-stationarity, so it pretrains the player DQN and only then trains the balancing agent to control gravity and maintain a 50% win-rate target.
evidence: The exact co-adaptation stability problem is visible in current game-DDA literature as a practical obstacle.
limitation: It avoids rather than characterizes simultaneous adaptation; no stability region, oscillation criterion, delay/noise robustness analysis or coupled-learning theorem is reported.

work: Repairing General Game Descriptions
method: Defines minimal repairs for faulty GDL descriptions, gives complexity results and ASP encoding.
evidence: Formal verification has progressed from detection to automatic repair of game descriptions.
limitation: Targets logical requirements of GDL descriptions, not learned procedural transfer.

work: Empowering Economic Simulation for Massively Multiplayer Online Games through Generative Agent-Based Modeling
area: MMO economy / generative agent-based modeling / player heterogeneity
method: KDD paper builds LLM-based MMO economic agents with profile, perception, memory, reasoning, action and reflection. Player profiles are derived from logs of 16,294 real players; simulations include trading/negotiation and rich/moderate/scarce resource regimes, reproducing role specialization and price/supply-demand behavior.
evidence: Modern MMO economy simulation already models heterogeneous player profiles, social trading and adaptive behavior rather than one fixed toy policy.
limitation: Agent reliability and simulation validity remain concerns; it does not establish robust economy-policy validity under arbitrary behavior-population shift.

work: Benchmarking World-Model Learning (WorldTest / AutumnBench)
method: Separates reward-free interaction from a scored test phase in related environments; AutumnBench includes planning, prediction and causal-dynamics-change tasks.
evidence: Behavior-based planning evaluation of learned world models is already a benchmark design principle.
limitation: Does not synthesize game-mechanic counterfactuals matched on true planning burden while separating sample-to-planning-adequacy burden.

work: Explicit Exploration for High-Welfare Equilibria in Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
method: Introduces explicit strategy exploration aimed at finding high-welfare equilibria in EGTA/MARL.
evidence: Even equilibrium-quality-aware strategy discovery is actively studied.
limitation: Not mechanic-controlled game design.

work: LADDER: Level Analysis Dataset for Difficulty Evaluation and Ranking
method: Combines objective player performance, level properties and perceived difficulty across multiple platformer games.
evidence: Cross-level/cross-game difficulty evaluation resources are expanding.
limitation: Dataset contribution, not agent-invariant theorem.

work: Boosting bug localization in software models of video games with simulations and component-specific genetic operations
method: Evolves game simulations to generate NPC traces and automatically localizes potential buggy model elements; component-specific genetic operators improve F-measure on commercial game Kromaia.
evidence: Trace-driven automated bug/failure localization in games is directly occupied, weakening broad failure-attribution/testing novelty claims.
limitation: Does not target causal attribution of PCG constraint failures or theorem-defined mechanic interactions, but it closes the broad 'game failure localization is missing' story.

work: Game Design Is Generative Design
method: Argues game design itself is generative design and reports surveys of 261 players and 126 designers; introduces procedural gameplay systems.
evidence: The design/PCG frontier increasingly treats generative systems as core game-design objects, not niche tools.
limitation: Conceptual/design framing, not a formal Game-AI gap.

work: PuzzlePlex: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Reasoning and Planning with Puzzles
method: 15 puzzle types, deterministic/stochastic and single/two-player settings; fine-grained reasoning/planning evaluation.
evidence: Cross-puzzle capability benchmarking is active.
limitation: Foundation-model evaluation, not representation-induced generation topology.

work: Benchmarking Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning with a Suite of Memory-Improvable Domains
method: Defines 'memory-improvable' domains via performance gaps under more vs less state information and builds POBAX benchmark.
evidence: A counterfactual/intervention-style memory-demand idea is already close to one G022 axis.
limitation: Broad RL benchmark, not a multidimensional game-level demand signature nor mechanic-to-demand causal study.

work: From Explainability to Interpretability: A Case Study on Game AI Using Program Synthesis
method: Doctoral line on symbolic programs for explaining/controlling game agents; explicitly identifies transferability of conceptual program libraries across game domains as an open research question.
evidence: Directly establishes that the G031 question is active and already owned by an ongoing research line.
limitation: Future-work/open-question statement, not yet a demonstrated solution in the retrieved literature.

work: Beyond Fixed Tasks: UED for Task-Level Pairs (ATLAS)
method: Generates joint autocurricula over reward-machine tasks and MiniGrid levels; structural mutations improve solvable challenging pairs.
evidence: Learned/algorithmic joint task+level generation is now closer to formal specification-conditioned design.
limitation: Still one environment family and trains/generates within the task-level space; no evidence of frozen designer transfer to unseen dynamics.

work: CHBench: A Cognitive Hierarchy Benchmark for Strategic Reasoning Capability of LLMs
method: Uses 15 normal-form games and cognitive hierarchy to estimate strategic-reasoning levels; studies memory/chat mechanisms.
evidence: Strategic-reasoning capability measurement using games is occupied.
limitation: LLM-centric and reasoning-depth focused; not general game-demand decomposition.

work: Nonogram: Complexity of Inference and Phase Transition Behavior
method: Proves Nonogram INFERENCE co-NP-complete, then empirically studies the same problem on random consistent boards. Uses 15×15, 20×20 and 25×25 boards, 250 boards per density; filled-cell density drives an inferability transition around 0.39–0.42 and normalized SAT propagation effort peaks near the transition.
evidence: A puzzle paper already combines a new complexity theorem with finite empirical phase-transition/hardness analysis on the same problem.
limitation: Rules/mechanics remain fixed; the treatment axis is instance density. It does not switch complexity-separating mechanics on/off on matched latent instances or estimate higher-order mechanic interactions.

work: Empirical Hardness in Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Research Challenges and Opportunities
method: Frames the gap between NP-hardness and instance-level hardness; highlights algorithm selection, hardness features, phase transitions/backbones and hard-instance generation.
evidence: Empirical hardness as a research program is active outside games.
limitation: MAPF, not formal game mechanics; no mechanic-complexity metatheorem bridge.

work: General Game Playing Hyper-Agents for Ludii
method: Predicts optimal sub-agent and heuristics for unseen Ludii games from ludemes/concepts; trained on 460 games and evaluated on 50 unseen games.
evidence: Algorithm selection from game descriptors is already directly mature in modern Ludii.
limitation: Does not concern mechanic-value robustness.

work: Benchmarking World-Model Learning (WorldTest / AutumnBench)
method: Separates reward-free interaction from evaluation in related environments and tests prediction, planning and changes to causal dynamics across interactive grid worlds.
evidence: World-model evaluation is moving toward downstream behavior and dynamics-change understanding rather than next-frame accuracy alone.
limitation: World-model learner/agent setting; not generation of target instances by a frozen learned designer.

work: Pixie: Code-Level Mechanic Generation for Game Designers
method: Generates/tests code-level mechanics directly inside annotated Unity projects and discusses developer perspectives.
evidence: Mechanic invention no longer requires bespoke research-only DSLs.
limitation: Poster-scale and developer-oriented; does not solve evaluator robustness.

work: Dice, Cards, Action! The Analysis, Play and Design of Multiplayer Tabletop Board Games with Monte Carlo Tree Search
method: PhD research line consolidating computational analysis of tabletop games using MCTS, including fingerprinting, skill depth and stochasticity.
evidence: A broad program of computational game characterization already exists and was extended through 2025.
limitation: MCTS/tabletop focused; does not replace controlled rule-intervention science.

work: A Generalized Bisimulation Metric of State Similarity between Markov Decision Processes
method: Defines a generalized bisimulation metric across pairs of MDPs and derives policy-transfer bounds and estimation results.
evidence: Cross-MDP structural similarity metrics and transfer analysis are increasingly mature.
limitation: Policy-transfer theory, not procedural-designer transfer or executable rule-conditioned generation.

work: Online Moderation in Competitive Action Games: How Intervention Affects Player Behaviors
method: Uses quasi-experimental causal inference on industry-scale Call of Duty moderation to estimate behavioral effects of intervention timing and severity.
evidence: Causal inference in live games is already real, rigorous and industry-scale.
limitation: Focuses moderation, not core mechanics; requires proprietary-scale telemetry.

work: Human adaptation to adaptive machines converges to game-theoretic equilibria
method: Empirically tests human-machine co-adaptation in general-sum games and shows machine learning rules can steer interactions toward predicted game-theoretic equilibria.
evidence: Co-adaptive human-machine equilibrium selection is a substantial existing research program.
limitation: Not video-game mechanic design specifically.

work: Encodings Effect on the Procedural Content Generation of Safari Rush Hour Puzzles
method: Compares two puzzle encodings (board-state vs piece-state) under three different metaheuristics and finds statistically significant fitness differences.
evidence: Representation × search-algorithm interaction in procedural puzzle generation is already directly studied.
limitation: Single sliding-puzzle family; no cross-family laws, landscape-mediated explanation, or held-out representation selection.

work: PuzzleJAX: A Benchmark for Reasoning and Learning
method: GPU-accelerated PuzzleScript-like DSL dynamically compiles games; validates several hundred PuzzleScript games and benchmarks tree search, RL and LLM reasoning.
evidence: Makes a compact executable puzzle DSL available for low-cost multi-game empirical research; strongly reduces G032 implementation risk for PuzzleScript-style mechanics.
limitation: Infrastructure, not a study of theorem-defined mechanic activation or representation selection.

work: A Markovian Framing of WaveFunctionCollapse for Procedurally Generating Aesthetically Complex Environments
method: Reframes WFC as an MDP and compares direct evolution with WFC-constrained optimization; also compares 1D vs 2D encodings of collapse sequences and explains different optimization behavior through mutation locality/cascading effects across multiple PCG objectives/domains.
evidence: Direct empirical representation → locality/stability/exploration → optimization-performance reasoning is already present in recent PCG.
limitation: Representations are not canonical semantically equivalent puzzle encodings under an equalized phenotype-edit neighborhood; no cross-puzzle held-out representation-selection boundary.

work: The Procedural Content Generation Benchmark: An Open-source Testbed for Generative Challenges in Games
method: Standardizes multiple PCG problems and evaluates Random, evolution strategy and genetic algorithm under quality/diversity/controllability objectives. Current repository includes macro-vs-tile variants for Lode Runner and Super Mario Bros.
evidence: Multi-problem standardized PCG comparison exists; representation/genotype size is already recognized as a possible source of difficulty.
limitation: Published default experiments do not appear to perform matched equivalent-representation × operator factorial analysis or held-out representation selection.

work: Hardness of Traversing Gadget Systems with Small Bandwidth
method: Shows PSPACE-hardness for several motion-planning gadget systems even when the connection graph has constant/small bandwidth; includes locking 2-toggles, doors and interacting reversible deterministic gadgets.
evidence: Worst-case hardness from interacting gadget semantics does not require globally wide/complex connection graphs.
limitation: Theory only; no empirical runtime/node-expansion or matched semantic-intervention experiment.

work: Landscape Features in Single-Objective Continuous Optimization: Have We Hit a Wall in Algorithm Selection Generalization?
method: Evaluates multiple landscape representations/features for algorithm selection under out-of-distribution problems and finds that on sufficiently OOD tests the selectors do not outperform a simple single-best-solver baseline.
evidence: Landscape-based selection often fails to generalize to genuinely unseen problem classes; leave-one-instance validation can be misleading.
limitation: Continuous black-box optimization and algorithm selection, not puzzle-PCG representation choice.

work: Transformer-Based Feature Learning for Algorithm Selection in Combinatorial Optimisation
method: Uses Essence high-level specifications and transformer-learned features to select the best combination of alternative Conjure-generated models/representations and solvers; evaluated on Car Sequencing, Covering Array and Social Golfers.
evidence: Automatic selection among alternative representations/viewpoints jointly with solvers across multiple combinatorial problem classes is already a peer-reviewed research task.
limitation: Target is solving runtime, not procedural generation quality/diversity; it does not isolate representation effects with matched semantic edit neighborhoods or study puzzle-PCG representations.

work: Code World Models for General Game Playing
area: Executable game world models / general game playing
method: Synthesizes executable Python game models from natural-language rules plus a few trajectories, then uses MCTS/ISMCTS for play across perfect- and imperfect-information games, including novel games.
evidence: Executable learned/synthesized game rule models are now a serious GGP artifact, making semantic model correctness operationally important.
limitation: Verification is contingent on synthesized-model correctness and relies on available trajectories/unit tests rather than adversarial minimal content+trace counterexamples.

work: SAGE: Semantic-Aware Regression Testing for Gray-Box Game Environments
method: Combines LLM-guided RL test generation, semantic multi-objective suite maintenance and update-log-aware prioritization in Overcooked and Minecraft.
evidence: Gray-box semantic regression generation, maintenance and version-aware test selection are rapidly becoming occupied.
limitation: Focuses coverage/bug detection and update relevance, not identity/equivalence of a particular exploit mechanism across changed dynamics.

work: Instructed Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning (IPCGRL)
method: Conditions an RL level generator on natural-language-like instructions and evaluates lexical/compositional generalization; near-OOD instructions transfer better than far-OOD or complex multitask conditions.
evidence: Instruction-conditioned PCGRL and zero/few-shot control generalization are directly occupied.
limitation: The game mechanics/domains are known during training; far-OOD semantic composition remains difficult.

work: Defying Gravity and Gadget Numerosity: The Complexity of the Hanano Puzzle and Beyond
method: Proves Hanano PSPACE-complete using visibility representations of NCL and a small base-gadget framework intended to generalize to irreversible-gravity games.
evidence: Hanano PSPACE-completeness and a reusable gravity-hardness framework are already established.
limitation: Theory only; does not measure practical state-space growth, shortest-solution horizons, carrying activation or empirical solver effort.

work: Closing the Loop: A Systematic Review of Experience-Driven Game Adaptation
method: PRISMA-style review of empirical closed-loop systems; notes limited full-loop integration, telemetry dominance, ML data/transparency challenges and underused affect sensing.
evidence: Adaptive-game research gaps increasingly concern sensing/experience validity rather than algorithm novelty.
limitation: Human/affective agenda is not ideal for a lightweight formal MSc thesis.

work: Dungeons & Replicants II: Automated Game Balancing Across Multiple Difficulty Dimensions via Deep Player Behavior Modeling
method: Uses generative player behavior models to reproduce strategies and identify class strengths/imbalances across combat challenges.
evidence: Balance conclusions already account for heterogeneous learned player behaviors.
limitation: Does not test approximation/surrogate decision equivalence against a true simulator under unseen policy populations.

work: Cross-environment Cooperation Enables Zero-shot Multi-agent Coordination
method: Uses procedural environment diversity to learn coordination behavior that transfers to unseen partners/environments.
evidence: Environment diversity and cross-environment ZSC are active, reducing novelty of generic cooperative transfer.
limitation: Does not isolate policy-invariant coordination descriptors of generated content.

work: Video Game Level Design as a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Problem
method: Formulates level generation as a multi-agent RL problem and evaluates generalization beyond training layouts.
evidence: Alternative generator decompositions and OOD level-shape generalization are active PCGRL topics.
limitation: Does not transfer a frozen learned designer to unseen rule/dynamics systems.

work: World and Human Action Models towards Gameplay Ideation (WHAM)
method: Generative world/action modeling for interactive gameplay ideation.
evidence: World models are moving from prediction toward interactive game creation/ideation.
limitation: High model/compute burden and no stable thesis gap from prediction alone.

work: Complexity of Jelly-No and Hanano Games with Various Constraints
method: Studies board-size/color restrictions; proves Jelly-No PSPACE-complete with unbounded colors and with one color plus black jellies, and gives additional NP-hard restricted Hanano/Jelly results.
evidence: The restriction lattice for these games is already being actively filled in by 2025–26 theory work.
limitation: No empirical finite-hardness study and no carrying-capacity activation experiment.

work: PuzzleJAX: A Benchmark for Reasoning and Learning
method: Compiles hundreds of PuzzleScript games into fast JAX environments and benchmarks tree search, PPO and LLM reasoning; supports custom rule DSLs.
evidence: Search-vs-learning differences across games and a suitable engine already exist.
limitation: Whole-game comparisons; no controlled mechanic-level planning/model-adequacy burden study.

work: Empirical Hardness in Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Research Challenges and Opportunities
method: Explicitly frames the gap between NP-hardness and individual-instance hardness; highlights structural predictors, phase transitions/backbones/backdoors, and hard-instance generation as research challenges.
evidence: Validates theory→empirical hardness→hard-instance generation as a legitimate research program.
limitation: Blue Sky agenda paper; MAPF rather than game mechanics.

work: SAGE: Semantic-Aware Gray-Box Game Regression Testing with Large Language Models
method: LLM-guided RL generates tests; semantic multiobjective optimization compresses suites; update logs prioritize tests across versions; evaluated on Overcooked Plus and Minecraft.
evidence: Semantic game regression generation/maintenance/prioritization is already directly occupied.
limitation: Preprint/current frontier; does not formalize build-invariant exploit mechanisms or minimal causal witnesses.

work: Video Game Level Design as a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Problem
method: Frames level design as MARL; reduces reward-computation bottleneck and improves OOD map-shape generalization via local/modular policies.
evidence: Distributed/multi-agent PCGRL and OOD shape generalization are occupied.
limitation: Generator architecture paper, not causal/content-theory contribution.

work: Assessing Adaptive World Models in Machines with Novel Games
method: Proposes suites of continually novel games as an evaluation paradigm for rapid world-model construction/refinement and metrics for sample-efficient adaptation.
evidence: Novel-game world-model induction is a recognized research target, not a niche game-engine problem.
limitation: Perspective/benchmark proposal; does not define content-conditioned equivalence or generate discriminating experiments for competing rule hypotheses.

work: Game Balancing via Procedural Content Generation and Simulations
method: Develops domain-independent PCG approaches for balanced levels/economies; explicitly notes transferability and simulation cost as limitations.
evidence: Simulation expense is a live game-design bottleneck and motivates surrogate/approximate simulation research.
limitation: Doctoral-consortium scope; no strategic decision-fidelity analysis of surrogates.

work: Embedded Mechanics Generation
method: Generates mechanics, reconstructs levels and creates enemies that require generated mechanics; compares RL/static agents and proposes Design Impact Accuracy.
evidence: Mechanic generation + mechanic-supporting content/evaluation are already direct research objects.
limitation: Ongoing/doctoral-style work; does not formalize finite complexity activation or invariant semantics.

work: Empirical Hardness in Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Research Challenges and Opportunities
