method: Frames algorithm selection, structural instance features, phase-transition/backbone/backdoor analysis, and hard/diverse instance generation as open empirical-hardness directions.
evidence: The forward characterize-hardness → inverse hard-instance-generation research arc is already recognized outside games.
limitation: Blue-sky/challenges paper rather than a completed mechanic-interaction study; no matched rule ablations.

work: Hardness of Traversing Gadget Systems with Small Bandwidth
method: Shows PSPACE-completeness for several gadget systems even at constant bandwidth, hence constant pathwidth/treewidth/cliquewidth; DAG gadgets provide a positive FPT family.
evidence: Strongly limits any generic 'low treewidth makes game search easy' claim.
limitation: Different gadget systems; does not invalidate bounded-treewidth WRP on a proven restricted macrofamily.

work: PandaSkill - Player Performance and Skill Rating in Esports: Application to League of Legends
area: Esports skill rating / Bayesian rating / temporal meta shift
method: Combines role-specific ML performance scores with OpenSkill and contextual/meta regional ratings over five years of professional LoL. The paper notes frequent balance updates/new mechanics and uses rolling temporal evaluation to account for gradual rating-distribution and possible meta shifts.
evidence: Modern esports skill ratings already model roles, regions, individual contribution and temporal evaluation.
limitation: It does not test whether the score scale itself is invariant across patches or decompose observed rating change into true skill change versus measurement-function drift.

work: Seeding for Success: Skill and Stochasticity in Tabletop Games
method: Separates skill-related performance from stochasticity and random sources.
evidence: Randomness/stochasticity dimension is already explicitly studied.
limitation: Does not cover memory, hidden-information reasoning, opponent modelling, etc.

work: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
method: Teacher uses transition-prediction error + co-learnability to build curricula.
evidence: Modern UED models task relationships explicitly to improve student OOD generalization.
limitation: Still evaluates curriculum/student generalization; no formal-spec-only frozen designer transfer.

work: URS: A Unified Neural Routing Solver for Cross-Problem Zero-Shot Generalization
method: One solver for >100 VRP variants; unseen variants zero-shot; raw constraints converted to executable masks.
evidence: Single model + variable constraints + executable masking + zero-shot is established on solver side.
limitation: VRP-family solver; not frozen learned content/instance designer across different game dynamics.

work: UniCO: Towards a Unified Model for Combinatorial Optimization Problems
method: Transformer trained across 10 CO problems; reports few-shot/zero-shot generalization.
evidence: One parameter set across heterogeneous CO problems is no longer a novelty claim.
limitation: Solver-side and trajectory/token formulation; not generation of new instances/content under unseen dynamics.

work: GOAL: A Generalist Combinatorial Optimization Agent Learner
method: Single shared backbone across routing, scheduling and graph problems; lightweight problem-specific adapters.
evidence: Heterogeneous multi-problem generalist neural solving is established.
limitation: New problems still use adapters/fine-tuning; not target-zero designer transfer.

work: Towards a Generic Representation of Combinatorial Problems for Learning-Based Approaches
method: Constraint AST/graph representation and GNN over XCSP3 constraints.
evidence: Generic graph encoding of formal constraints is established.
limitation: Representation alone does not solve zero-target procedural generation across formal dynamics.

work: The SIDO Performance Model for League of Legends
area: Esports analytics / skill measurement / longitudinal stability
method: Hierarchical Bayesian LoL performance model explicitly evaluates metric discrimination, independence and stability. It states that stability should assure a metric measures the same thing from patch to patch, then compares rankings from patches 13.6-13.9 versus 13.14-13.18 using concordance indices.
evidence: Patch-to-patch stability of esports performance metrics is directly occupied.
limitation: Concordance cannot identify whether rank change is true player-skill change or a patch-induced change in the measurement function/construct. No explicit measurement-invariance or scale-linking test is reported.

work: Skill Depth in Tabletop Board Games
method: Expands/tunes MCTS algorithmic space and measures skill traces under different configurations.
evidence: Shows game skill-depth conclusions depend on algorithmic space; motivates multiple resource/capability axes.
limitation: Still centered on MCTS/configuration; does not establish a general multidimensional capability fingerprint.

work: Sturgeon-MKIV: Constraint-Based Level and Playthrough Generation with Graph Label Rewrite Rules
method: Generates graph-based levels and example playthroughs jointly using graph label rewrite mechanics.
evidence: Solvability-by-construction with explicit mechanics/playthrough generation is established beyond simple 2D grids.
limitation: Demonstrated on a limited set of graph-based games; scalability/generality remain practical issues.

work: GAVEL: Generating Games Via Evolution and Language Models
method: Uses Ludii rule code, evolutionary computation and language models to mutate/recombine mechanics and generate novel games.
evidence: Whole-game/rule generation in a broad formal game language is active modern prior art.
limitation: Evaluation of originality/quality remains difficult; LLM/evolution machinery is not suitable novelty by itself.

work: Adaptive Measurement of Change in the Context of Item Parameter Drift
area: Psychometrics / latent change / item parameter drift
method: Simulation study shows that item-parameter drift can create false or distorted estimates of intra-individual latent change and recommends checking item stability before interpreting change.
evidence: The exact statistical danger motivating G070 is already known in psychometrics.
limitation: No esports or game-patch application; game telemetry does not map trivially to conventional test items.

work: Safe Learning of PDDL Domains with Conditional Effects
method: Proves that learning non-trivial safe action models with conditional effects may require exponentially many samples, then gives tractable conditions and Conditional-SAM.
evidence: Specific operator constructs can provably make model learning hard.
limitation: Does not ask whether the same operator simultaneously changes true-game planning/search burden.

work: Sample-Efficient Quality-Diversity by Cooperative Coevolution
method: Improves QD sample efficiency by decomposing the search problem; evaluated in QDAX tasks.
evidence: Sample-efficient QD itself is an active method contribution and should not be reinvented.
limitation: Policy-QD setting, not game-instance matched-burden synthesis.

work: Map Connectivity and Empirical Hardness of Grid-based Multi-Agent Pathfinding Problem
method: Studies normalized-Laplacian λ₂ versus solver hardness and uses QD to generate maps in target λ₂ ranges; relation is not strictly monotonic.
evidence: Strong neighboring example of structural finite-hardness analysis plus generator-driven instance design.
limitation: MAPF, not games; no theorem-defined mechanic ablations.

work: PCGRL+: Scaling, Control and Generalization in Reinforcement Learning Level Generators
method: JAX/GPU PCGRL; randomized sizes and frozen pinpoints; evaluates large OOD map sizes and robust design strategies.
evidence: Scaling, control and OOD size generalization are explicit PCGRL research targets already.
limitation: Does not address theorem-linked counterfactual mechanic hardness.

work: Know Your Bugs: A Survey of Issues in Automated Game Testing Literature
method: Literature review with open/axial coding; taxonomy of 26 automated-game-testing issues in five higher-level categories.
evidence: Confirms game testing is a substantial established research area with multiple issue categories rather than an empty application niche.
limitation: Taxonomy/review, not a method for causal counterexamples or rule-interaction attribution.

work: Hamiltonian Paths and Cycles in NP-Complete Puzzles
method: Shows Hamiltonian path/cycle on grid graphs of maximum degree 3 is an effective NP-completeness source and applies it to multiple grid puzzles.
evidence: Provides a clean grid-native source problem that can eliminate the orthogonal-embedding burden in a Bloxorz theorem-derived generator.
limitation: Theory only; no finite mechanic-factorial experiment.

work: Procedurally Puzzling: On Algorithmic Difficulty and Player Experience in QD-Generated Logic Grid Puzzles
area: Puzzle PCG / quality diversity / solver difficulty
method: Uses constrained MAP-Elites to generate solvable logic-grid puzzles spanning algorithmic difficulty and studies the relation between solver loops and player-reported difficulty.
evidence: Using solver effort as a generation target and generating diverse puzzles across difficulty levels are already published.
limitation: One puzzle family and one difficulty proxy; it does not optimize a counterfactual mechanic-interaction contrast or test robustness across held-out solver families.

work: Advanced Spikes `n' Stuff: An NP-Hard Puzzle Game in Which All Tutorials Are Efficiently Solvable
method: Full-proof reread v34: ASnS({h,s}) is polynomial because all reachable 'tame' states form a polynomial-size state space when no vertical crossbows exist. ASnS({s,v}) allows exponentially many persistent vertical-crossbow flags but is polynomial via monotone deactivation: repeatedly deactivate a reachable vertical crossbow and safely retrace to the start. ASnS({h,v}) uses the same high-level strategy but repairs reverse walks by timing-adjustment moves. Full {h,s,v} is NP-complete using one-way, variable, clause and crossover gadgets; vertical-crossbow deactivation provides persistent state used to unlock clauses/crossovers.
evidence: The paper owns the 3-way asymptotic interaction and shows that the strict-subset polynomial algorithms rely on different state-space compression/retrace arguments.
limitation: No empirical finite I3, no scaling law, and no test of whether failure of those subset-specific certificates predicts solver effort.

work: Procedural Content Generation in Games: A Survey with Insights on Emerging LLM Integration
method: Reviews roughly two hundred recent PCG studies and maps methods, representations, evaluation and emerging LLM integration.
evidence: Broad PCG, PCGML, RL-based generation and representation research are mature and rapidly diversifying.
limitation: A survey does not resolve the narrow causal or transfer-boundary questions in G029/T002.

work: Rethinking Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment for Video Game Design
method: Peer-reviewed conceptual audit: rethinks DDA's foundations, challenges overreliance on Flow theory, redefines DDA in terms of game difficulty, and proposes a goal-based six-step design process.
evidence: Generic DDA framing/design and the need for explicit objectives are established; a new adaptive controller alone is weak novelty.
limitation: Does not derive stability/instability of a coupled adapting-player/controller feedback loop.

work: Surrogate-assisted Monte Carlo Tree Search for Real-time Video Games
method: Uses surrogate assistance to accelerate MCTS in real-time games.
evidence: Surrogate models also already appear on the gameplay-planning side, not only design/PCG.
limitation: Planning speed/performance rather than fidelity of downstream game-design/equilibrium conclusions.

work: Data-driven Decision-Focused Surrogate Modeling
method: Learns surrogates for accurate decisions rather than globally accurate predictions in optimization settings.
evidence: Generic decision-focused surrogate training is established outside games.
limitation: Does not model strategic re-equilibration/game-specific exploitability.

work: Noisy Zero-Shot Coordination: Breaking the Common Knowledge Assumption in Zero-Shot Coordination Games
method: Formulates ZSC where agents observe noisy versions of the underlying Dec-POMDP; reduces to a meta-Dec-POMDP and trains across problem distributions.
evidence: ZSC already extends beyond unseen partners to uncertain problem specifications.
limitation: Does not answer policy-invariant content-property identification.

work: Robust Losses for Decision-Focused Learning
method: Studies robust losses for predict-then-optimize/decision-focused learning.
evidence: The broader DFL methodology is mature and provides baselines.
limitation: No game-theoretic re-adaptation focus.

work: On Video Game Balancing: Joining Player- and Data-Driven Analytics
method: Combines a survey of 680 participants with more than four million Guild Wars 2 combat records to compare player-driven notions of balance with telemetry-derived analytics. Shows that 'balance' is multi-dimensional and stakeholder-dependent rather than a single win-rate target, and argues that balancing should be tailored to the actual player base.
evidence: Player-aware/data-aware balance definitions and large-scale telemetry analysis are established; generic 'balance should account for different players' is not novel.
limitation: Requires large real-player data and does not define a robust parameter-space balance region under uncertain/evolving strategy populations.

work: Scaling, Control and Generalization in Reinforcement Learning Level Generators
method: Scales JAX-based PCGRL training to very large experience budgets and evaluates control/generalization to unseen map sizes and shapes; local observations materially improve OOD behavior.
evidence: OOD size/shape generalization of RL content generators is directly studied.
limitation: Unseen geometry/scale is not unseen executable dynamics, and no zero-target frozen designer protocol is tested.

work: Advanced Spikes 'n' Stuff: An NP-Hard Puzzle Game in Which All Tutorials Are Efficiently Solvable
method: Defines three trap mechanics h,s,v such that the full combination is NP-complete while every strict subset is polynomial-time solvable.
evidence: Provides an unusually clean formal non-additive mechanic interaction: hardness exists only through the combination of all three mechanics.
limitation: Theory only; does not measure finite-instance empirical hardness, solver effort distributions, phase transition, or practical activation of the theorem.

work: Action Model Learning with Guarantees
method: Develops sound/complete action-model learning guarantees and convergence-style results from examples.
evidence: Version-space/action-model identification with guarantees already exists.
limitation: Does not use game-content grammars as a restricted intervention/query space.

work: On the Evaluation of Procedural Level Generation Systems
method: Builds an evaluation taxonomy and finds lack of robust, generalisable, widely accepted PCG evaluation practice.
evidence: Evaluator dependence is a real methodological problem.
limitation: Does not define a new agent-invariant content-property theory.

work: Literally Unplayable: On Constraint-Based Generation of Uncompletable Levels
method: Generates intentionally uncompletable levels and describes generating levels that require use of a special move.
evidence: Counterfactual mechanic necessity in generated levels already has a direct precedent.
limitation: Does not study complexity-class interaction/finite hardness.

work: Predicting Solvability and Difficulty of Sokoban Puzzles
method: Uses learned surrogates to predict Sokoban solvability and push-count difficulty from puzzle boards.
evidence: Empirical puzzle difficulty prediction is occupied within individual puzzle domains.
limitation: Does not relate empirical difficulty to complexity-inducing mechanic subsets or cross-game transfer.

work: Cross-Paradigm Modelling: A Study of Puzznic
method: Compares constraint programming and AI planning models of Puzznic, identifies complementary strengths/weaknesses, and uses the constraint model for parameterized puzzle-instance generation.
evidence: Comparing alternative modelling paradigms for a puzzle and exploiting one for generation is already occupied.
limitation: Single puzzle family; does not perform matched multi-family representation × generator experiments or held-out representation selection.

work: On Generalization for Generative Flow Networks
method: Formalizes GFlowNet generalization and studies the ability to reach unseen parts of the reward space, especially length generalization.
evidence: Generic GFlowNet generalization is already a research topic.
limitation: Does not train one instance generator across formal schemas then frozen-transfer it to unseen operator/dynamics semantics.

work: GAVEL: Generating Games Via Evolution and Language Models
method: Uses LLM/evolution in Ludii to generate novel board games beyond the training-rule space.
evidence: Large-scale automated game invention in expressive rule languages is already current frontier.
limitation: Evaluation of generated-game quality remains hard, but generation itself is occupied.

work: Treatment Effect Estimation Amidst Dynamic Network Interference in Online Gaming Experiments
method: Develops treatment-effect estimation for online games when multiplayer interactions create transient network interference that violates standard SUTVA-style independence; evaluates the method on real mobile-game experimental data.
evidence: Interference-aware causal experimentation in online gaming is already a direct methodological contribution.
limitation: Focuses treatment-effect estimation rather than game-balance boundary robustness, but closes a generic 'network-aware LiveOps A/B testing' thesis.

work: Autoverse: An Evolvable Game Language for Learning Robust Embodied Agents
method: Uses an evolvable rule language to evolve increasingly complex environments/playtraces and then continue open-ended RL via environments maximizing value-function error.
evidence: Rules+maps as curriculum/environment search are already active.
limitation: Does not study theorem-defined mechanic interaction like G032.

work: Generalized Response Objectives for Strategy Exploration in Empirical Game-Theoretic Analysis
method: Studies response objectives that explicitly alter strategy exploration/discovered strategy sets in empirical game-theoretic analysis.
evidence: Strategy discovery is an explicit research object in modern EGTA/PSRO.
limitation: Does not use matched game-mechanic interventions.

work: GAVEL: Generating Games Via Evolution and Language Models
method: Fine-tunes CodeLlama on 574 Ludii games, holds out 14 games, then initializes MAP-Elites with the full held-out game descriptions and mutates their code to generate novel games.
evidence: A learned game mutator can operate on games completely held out from model training.
limitation: The full target game artifact is supplied at deployment and target-time evolutionary search/evaluation lasts hundreds of steps; this is not spec-only generation and not zero target search.

work: Sliding Puzzles Gym: A Scalable Benchmark for State Representation in Visual Reinforcement Learning
method: Controls observation diversity while holding transition dynamics/action space fixed, isolating representation-learning difficulty in sliding puzzles.
evidence: Controlled representation studies in puzzle RL already exist.
limitation: Observation representation for acting agents, not generator genotype/encoding and operator interaction.

work: On Automating Video Game Regression Testing by Planning and Learning
area: Automated game testing / action-model learning / PDDL
method: Learns a PDDL action model of gameplay mechanics from detailed game logs, incrementally checks consistency, and uses planning to generate regression-test scripts. Demonstrated on Unity Creator Kit RPG. Full text notes that learned models can need manual correction and that logging abstraction/generalization are major challenges.
evidence: Learning formal game mechanics from playtraces and using them for regression testing is directly occupied.
limitation: Does not establish a new general theory of game-mechanic identifiability; it relies on sufficient developer-guided logging and gameplay coverage.

work: Action Model Learning with Guarantees
area: Planning / action model learning / version spaces
method: Develops a version-space theory for fully observable action-model learning, maintains all consistent solutions, constructs sound/complete approximations, and proves convergence to the true transition model with sufficient examples.
evidence: Identifiability/version-space guarantees for action-model learning are mature outside games.
limitation: Not a game-specific patch-change diagnosis study under constrained interfaces.

work: Multi-Task Learning for Routing Problem with Cross-Problem Zero-Shot Generalization
method: Represents VRP variants as combinations of shared attributes; one model solves seen and unseen combinations.
evidence: Cross-problem zero-shot compositional generalization with one neural solver is established.
limitation: Restricted to related VRP family; solver, not instance/content generator.

work: Learning Abstract World Models for Value-preserving Planning with Options
method: Learns abstract MDPs with conditions ensuring planning induces bounded value loss; reports improved planning/learning sample efficiency.
evidence: Value-preserving learned abstractions for planning are established beyond classic VE work.
limitation: No mechanic-intervention causal design or true-search/model-burden decomposition.

work: GenCO: Generating Diverse Designs with Combinatorial Constraints
method: Deep generative model integrated with combinatorial solver; includes game-level/map generation.
evidence: Neural constrained generation and solver-integrated feasibility are established.
limitation: Does not establish frozen cross-domain designer transfer to unseen executable dynamics.

work: GEEvo: Game Economy Generation and Balancing with Evolutionary Algorithms
method: Full-paper audit: represents economies as source/random-gate/pool/converter/drain graphs; uses one EA to generate valid economy graphs and another to tune edge weights against simulated resource objectives. 194/200 generated economies were valid. The paper explicitly notes that its example player behaves like a spammer and proposes multiple small bots with different strategies as future work; it also proposes studying positive-feedback loops.
evidence: Economy generation, simulation-driven balancing and parameter optimization are occupied.
limitation: Player-strategy robustness and feedback stability are not solved, but they are explicit/obvious next directions of the paper.

work: A Framework for Predicting the Impact of Game Balance Changes through Meta Discovery
method: Full-text/current audit v35: develops Meta Discovery in Pokémon Showdown using an RL battle agent, adaptive team-building, and simulation to predict how balance changes alter the metagame. The framework can start from scratch and update team pick/win/popularity statistics as strategies evolve. A key limitation is player-skill coverage: the paper explicitly notes that metagames differ by skill level and proposes a swarm of agents with varying skill levels as future work.
evidence: Dynamic strategic response to balance patches and automated metagame discovery are directly occupied; fixed-strategy evaluation is not the whole field.
limitation: One game ecosystem and limited player-skill representation. Population-robust balance regions under explicit evaluator/skill/agent-population uncertainty are not established here, but varying-skill populations are an explicit author future-work direction.

work: Autoverse: An Evolvable Game Language for Learning Robust Embodied Agents
method: DSL of cellular-automaton rewrite mechanics; evolves rules and initial maps to create increasingly complex environments and trains agents.
evidence: Evolvable formal game rules + maps for curriculum are established.
limitation: Evolves environments for student learning; not a pretrained frozen level-designer policy transferred to an unseen rule system.

work: LLMArena: Assessing Capabilities of LLMs in Dynamic Multi-Agent Environments
method: Seven games assess spatial reasoning, planning, numerical reasoning, risk, communication, opponent modelling and collaboration.
evidence: A named multidimensional capability vector over game environments already exists for LLM evaluation.
limitation: Scores agent capabilities; does not estimate how much each GAME demands a capability under controlled resource removal.

work: TeamCraft: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Systems in Minecraft
method: 55k task variants, procedural expert demonstrations, generalization to novel goals/scenes/unseen agent counts.
evidence: Team-size/generalization benchmarking in cooperative game environments is active.
limitation: Minecraft/agent-centric; not PCG science about coordination-demand preservation.

work: Who Needs to Know? Minimal Knowledge for Optimal Coordination
method: Defines strategically relevant vs irrelevant teammate information and computes compact representations by Bellman backup.
evidence: Information dependence for optimal coordination is formally occupied.
limitation: Overcooked-focused analysis; not procedural generation of content profiles.

work: Hypernetworks for Zero-Shot Transfer in Reinforcement Learning (HyperZero)
method: Hypernetwork maps MDP task parameters to value functions/policies; zero-shot new reward/transition conditions.
evidence: Formal/context-conditioned zero-shot policy generation is established.
limitation: Task parameterization is structured and policy is an acting agent, not a procedural designer in a new game-rule system.

work: One Model, Any CSP: Graph Neural Networks as Fast Global Search Heuristics for Constraint Satisfaction
method: Uses one generic GNN architecture/representation across CSPs of different arity, relations and domain sizes as a learned search heuristic.
evidence: One-model formal graph machinery across heterogeneous constraint problems is occupied on the solver side.
limitation: Search/solver heuristic rather than generator of new problem instances for unseen schemas.

work: Population-based Evaluation in Repeated Rock-Paper-Scissors as a Benchmark for Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
method: Evaluates agents against a population of 43 RPS tournament bots and argues that single-expert/head-to-head evaluation is insufficient; uses population returns and exploitability.
evidence: Population-based agent evaluation in games is already an explicit, peer-reviewed methodology before G049.
limitation: Agent evaluation only; does not attribute value to individual game mechanics or study mechanic-level Shapley sign stability.

work: Strategy Extraction for Transfer in AI Agents
method: Extracts recurring behavioural action-sequence strategies from existing knowledge for transfer/generalisation; demonstrated in Pacman and a dungeon crawler.
evidence: Behavioural strategy extraction for reuse across contexts is occupied.
limitation: Not symbolic rule/program invariants across formal game-rule changes; transfer characterization is preliminary.

work: Bilevel Entropy based Mechanism Design for Balancing Meta in Video Games
area: Game-theoretic balance / mechanism design / equilibrium meta
method: AAMAS paper treats game balancing as bilevel mechanism design: an upper-level designer changes game parameters while the lower level recomputes strategic response/mixed-strategy equilibrium; the objective promotes a high-entropy meta. Experiments include abstract and Pokémon-style competitive settings.
evidence: Re-equilibrating strategic response after a balance change is established; balance optimization need not assume a fixed policy population.
limitation: The strategy/game model is still an explicit modeled population/strategy space; it does not quantify how the acceptable balance region deforms as evaluator populations or discovered strategy sets change.

work: Traversability, Reconfiguration, and Reachability in the Gadget Framework
method: Shows complexity can depend strongly on the objective: for reversible deterministic gadgets, reachability with non-interacting tunnels is easy while interacting tunnels is hard, but reconfiguration can be PSPACE-complete even for some non-interacting gadgets.
evidence: The interacting-vs-non-interacting dichotomy is objective-specific rather than a universal statement about 'gadget difficulty'.
limitation: Theory only; no matched empirical activation study.

work: Measuring Board Game Distance
method: Measures distances between games using concept vectors and compares metrics; discusses limits of ludemes/concepts and subjectivity/context.
evidence: Game-distance construction is established in Ludii.
limitation: Distance is not the same as a causal/signed rule-change explanation of transfer outcomes.

work: Tools for Landscape Analysis of Optimisation Problems in Procedural Content Generation for Games
method: Applies diagonal walks, high-level landscape-property estimation and problem-similarity measures to search-based PCG; demonstrates on Mario/GBEA and explicitly discusses using landscape knowledge to choose PCG components including representations and optimizers.
evidence: Landscape analysis for understanding PCG and informing representation/algorithm choices is already explicitly proposed.
limitation: Primarily a vision/tutorial plus example analysis; not a multi-representation causal factorial, not puzzle-focused, and no held-out representation-selection experiment.

work: Towards a General Transfer Approach for Policy-Value Networks
method: Transfers fully convolutional AlphaZero-style policy-value networks across games and variants using shared Ludii semantics; evaluates zero-shot and fine-tuned transfer.
evidence: Direct large-scale game/variant transfer evidence already exists, including negative-transfer cases.
limitation: Does not formulate a controlled signed semantic rule-change × transferred-component causal law.

work: Sturgeon-MKIII: Simultaneous Level and Example Playthrough Generation via Constraint Satisfaction with Tile Rewrite Rules
method: Generates tile-based game levels and example playthroughs simultaneously using constraint satisfaction and tile rewrite rules, thereby guaranteeing at least one mechanics-consistent completion trace.
evidence: Joint synthesis of initial content and an action/playthrough witness under one formal rule model is already established.
limitation: It does not compare two competing rule models, synthesize behavioral counterexamples, or certify bounded equivalence.

work: GameRTS: A Regression Testing Framework for Video Games
method: Builds state-transition graphs tied to game assets/design/source changes and selects affected regression traces across commercial game versions; reports all evaluation bugs detected and two new critical bugs.
evidence: Game-specific regression-test selection and change-impact analysis are established at ICSE.
limitation: Primarily selects/adapts existing tests; not semantic equivalence of a known exploit mechanism when trajectories cease to replay.

work: Learning Properties in Simulation-Based Games
method: Learns approximate utilities of simulation-based games and extends uniform-approximation guarantees to regret, equilibrium-related and welfare properties; discusses instability of welfare-optimal equilibria and stable alternatives.
evidence: Direct mathematical collision with the naive G037 claim that approximate simulators need equilibrium/property fidelity guarantees.
limitation: Works on empirical games/utility approximation rather than an extrapolative surrogate jointly over game-design parameters and unseen policy discovery.

work: Learning of Generalizable and Interpretable Knowledge in Grid-Based Reinforcement Learning Environments
method: Uses DreamCoder-style program synthesis to imitate RL policies and inspect learned concept libraries across navigation and miniature Atari-style games.
evidence: Interpretable concept extraction across multiple game-like domains is established.
limitation: Does not demonstrate systematic cross-game transfer of concept libraries or characterize transfer boundaries.

work: Synthesis of Procedural Models for Deterministic Transition Systems
method: Synthesizes executable procedural state-transition models from state-action-next-state examples across target formalisms such as STRIPS and cellular automata.
evidence: Executable transition-model induction from examples is generic planning/program-synthesis prior.
limitation: Does not actively synthesize game content/queries to distinguish hypotheses or define game-content-relative behavioral equivalence.

work: Synthesizing Reactive Test Environments for Autonomous Systems: Testing Reach-Avoid Specifications with Multi-Commodity Flows
method: Synthesizes reactive environmental constraints that force target test behavior while preserving feasibility, using multi-commodity flows and bilevel optimization.
evidence: Environment generation can be reactive and formally optimized; generic environment-as-experiment is mature.
limitation: Not learned game-rule fidelity and not PCG semantics, but methodologically very close to G036's original environment-query idea.

work: CSP beyond tractable constraint languages
method: Extends backdoor depth to CSP and proves FPT for finite tractable semi-conservative base languages parameterized by backdoor depth plus domain size.
evidence: Distance-to-tractability has mature refined measures beyond simple backdoor size.
limitation: Not a game-specific mechanic parameter and does not test empirical solver effort.

work: Predicting the Empirical Hardness of Metric TSP Instances
method: Uses >45k metric TSP instances and branch-and-bound nodes to label/predict easy vs hard instances from cost-matrix features.
evidence: Shows deterministic solver work counters and structural hardness prediction are established in combinatorial optimization.
limitation: No matched mechanism intervention or game content.

work: Learning Parameterized Families of Games
method: Environment parameters become regressor inputs for deviation payoffs/equilibria across a family.
evidence: Thorough analysis of strategic incentives over continuous/discrete parameter spaces is already a research object.
limitation: Not a formal mechanic-topology phase-transition study, but directly crowds generic phase-map claims.

work: MCU: A Task-centric Framework for Open-ended Agent Evaluation in Minecraft
method: Six task difficulty dimensions; task-space analysis for Minecraft agents.
evidence: Multi-dimensional task/capability characterization exists in open-ended agent evaluation.
limitation: Dimensions are task-level and include subjective/semantic notions such as creativity/novelty; not intrinsic game computational-demand fingerprint.

work: Strategic Knowledge Transfer
method: Transfers response strategies across related games/opponents to accelerate PSRO.
evidence: Strategic knowledge transfer across changing game conditions is established.
limitation: Transfers player responses, not procedural content designers.

work: MAESTRO: Open-Ended Environment Design for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
method: Joint curriculum over environment parameters and co-player policies.
evidence: Open-ended environment design extends to competitive multi-agent games.
limitation: No direct evidence of one frozen teacher transferred across unseen rule systems.

work: Reasoning about Causality in Games
method: Introduces structural causal games / mechanised games, supporting prediction, intervention and counterfactual queries over game variables and strategies.
evidence: Causal reasoning in games is formally established; generic 'apply causality to games' is not novel.
limitation: Framework-level contribution; does not study controlled videogame-mechanic perturbations across multiple solvers.

work: Compositional Diffusion-Based Continuous Constraint Solvers (Diffusion-CCSP)
method: Factor-graph formulation; compose energies of diffusion models trained for individual constraint types.
evidence: Strong generalization to novel combinations of known constraints.
limitation: Known-constraint composition, not new primitive semantics; outputs are CCSP solutions, not game-level instance designers across rule systems.

work: MDP Playground: An Analysis and Debug Testbed for Reinforcement Learning
method: Provides independently controllable hardness dimensions and interaction studies across toy and wrapped environments.
evidence: Orthogonal hardness control and multidimensional environment difficulty are established.
limitation: Abstract MDP knobs; does not isolate semantic executable game mechanics or world-model adequacy burden.

work: Anomaly Detection in the Open World: Normality Shift Detection, Explanation, and Adaptation
method: NDSS work formalizes and detects 'normality shift' in zero-positive anomaly detection, explains the shift and adapts the model using long-term security datasets.
evidence: Detect-explain-adapt under normal-behavior drift is established security methodology.
limitation: Not game anti-cheat; no game-patch/player-meta experiment.

work: Policy Space Diversity for Non-Transitive Games
method: Defines a policy diversity metric whose improvement guarantees better Nash approximation; integrates it into PSRO.
evidence: Rigorous strategic diversity metrics tied to equilibrium quality are established.
limitation: Population/policy-side diversity, not game-mechanic-induced option diversity.

work: Deep Explainable Relational Reinforcement Learning: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach
method: Learns interpretable logical-rule policies and demonstrates generalization to modified configurations in several domains.
evidence: Logical rule policies that generalize under environment modifications are established.
limitation: Mostly within-domain structural changes; not cross-game concept-library transfer under distinct rule systems.

work: Mechanic Maker 2.0: Reinforcement Learning for Evaluating Generated Rules
method: Replaces a static A* approximator with RL for generated-rule evaluation and finds that RL produces distinct sets of rules, potentially more usable by humans.
evidence: Direct evidence that changing evaluator class changes what rules/mechanics an AGD system selects.
limitation: Does not systematically quantify sign/rank stability of individual mechanic value across evaluator populations.

work: Procedural Content Generation via Knowledge Transformation (PCG-KT)
method: Formalizes PCG via transferring/transforming knowledge across domains and surveys transfer learning and blending between games.
evidence: Cross-domain PCG knowledge transfer is established as a research framing.
limitation: Surveyed approaches typically adapt/retrain or combine known domains; does not establish frozen spec-only zero-target designer transfer to unseen executable dynamics.

work: Quality Diversity in the Amorphous Fortress (QD-AF): Evolving for Complexity in 0-Player Games
method: Uses quality diversity to generate 0-player game/environment families with emergent cooperative and competitive multi-agent dynamics.
evidence: Open-ended generation of strategically/ecologically varied rule systems is established.
limitation: Complexity descriptors are domain-specific and do not identify transferable procedural knowledge or intervention-defined game demands.

work: MDP Playground: An Analysis and Debug Testbed for Reinforcement Learning
method: Controls delayed rewards, reward density, sequence length, stochasticity, representations, irrelevant features and more; studies algorithm interactions on toy and complex environments.
evidence: Controlled environment-hardness dimensions and factor interactions are established outside specific game mechanics.
limitation: MDP meta-features are not the same as semantically meaningful game mechanics; focus is debugging RL agents rather than game science.

work: Environment Generation for Zero-Shot Compositional Reinforcement Learning (CoDE)
method: Generator agent builds compositional task graphs tailored to a learner.
evidence: Learned environment/task generator and compositional environment generation are established.
limitation: Reported zero-shot generalization is primarily the student policy; generator is not shown as frozen cross-dynamics designer.

work: Celeste is PSPACE-hard
method: Proves PSPACE-hardness in several different ways corresponding to different subsets of Celeste mechanics.
evidence: Complexity analysis over alternative mechanic subsets is active beyond classic games.
limitation: No empirical solver-hardness bridge.

work: Keke AI Competition: Solving puzzle levels in a dynamically changing mechanic space
area: Dynamic game mechanics / automated solving / game AI competition
method: Builds a Baba-is-You-style competition where rules can be created/broken during play. The framework supports multiple active rule types and evaluates BFS, DFS, best-first/default and random baselines on hidden levels; baseline solve rates range roughly 33–53%. Authors explicitly motivate adaptation to combinations of changing mechanics.
evidence: Solver performance across dynamically changing mechanic combinations is already an established Game AI benchmark object.
limitation: It does not use theorem-defined complexity classes, matched mechanic-subset counterfactuals, factorial/Möbius interaction estimands, or finite activation analysis.

work: Too much information: Why CDCL solvers need to forget learned clauses
method: Empirical SAT study encounters solver runs extending beyond practical limits, introduces explicit censoring/timeouts, and states that survival analysis is necessary for the censored runtime data.
evidence: Real solver-hardness studies already treat timeout censoring statistically rather than as a cosmetic benchmark detail.
limitation: SAT-specific and observational; no game-mechanic intervention.

work: Compressing and Comparing the Generative Spaces of Procedural Content Generators
method: Uses compression/dimensionality methods to compare PCG generative spaces across 2D tile-based game domains.
evidence: Generalizable comparison of generator spaces is an established goal; observed domain inconsistency.
limitation: Focuses generator outputs/spaces rather than controlled representation-induced search topology.

work: Market Interventions in a Large-Scale Virtual Economy
area: Virtual economy / causal inference / live-service intervention
method: Studies an Old School RuneScape transaction tax and item sink using real market data and causal inference. The tax did not meaningfully change volume at the tax boundaries; the item sink contributed to inflation of luxury-good prices without reducing trading volume.
evidence: Real causal evaluation of live-game economic policy interventions is already established.
limitation: Does not provide simulator-policy robustness to changing player-behavior populations.

work: Universally Hard Hamiltonian Cycle Problem Instances
method: Tests evolutionarily discovered hard Hamiltonian-cycle instances against six major backtracking algorithms and 91,000 randomized instances.
evidence: Some structured HC instances remain hard across multiple exact backtracking algorithms, while those instances are rare in large random ensembles.
limitation: Cross-backtracker hardness still does not prove algorithm-independent complexity, and the domain is general graphs rather than game instances.

work: MACQ: A Holistic View of Model Acquisition Techniques
method: Provides a common framework for generating traces and applying multiple action-model acquisition methods, including different trace-generation/sampling strategies.
evidence: Model acquisition pipelines and trace-generation design are mature enough to have general tooling.
limitation: Not a direct content-realizability study and not Game AI specific.

work: AdaRL: What, Where, and How to Adapt in Transfer Reinforcement Learning
method: Builds a structural environment model to locate changed mechanisms and derive minimal shared/domain-specific representations for adaptation.
evidence: Very close to 'which changed component should transfer/adapt?'
limitation: Not centered on interpretable game-mechanic/ludeme edits or policy-vs-value component transfer benchmark.

work: Automated Gameplay Testing and Validation with Curiosity-Conditioned Proximal Trajectories
method: Curiosity + imitation learning explores near expert trajectories; improves coverage and bug/design-issue discovery in complex 3D navigation; includes visual analytics.
evidence: RL exploration and bug discovery are established game-testing contributions.
limitation: Does not provide semantic causal attribution or cross-version equivalence.

work: Waypoint Routing on Bounded Treewidth Graphs
method: Improves WRP on treewidth tw to 2^{O(tw)}·n and proves ETH-optimality.
evidence: If the restricted Bloxorz↔WRP bridge is proven, macro-treewidth becomes a legitimate FPT tractability axis.
limitation: The theorem applies to WRP, not arbitrary Bloxorz gadget graphs.

work: The Hardest Hamiltonian Cycle Problem Instances: The Plateau of Yes and the Cliff of No
method: Evolves Hamiltonian-cycle graphs to maximize a specialized backtracking solver's recursion count and analyzes hard yes/no neighborhoods and structural plateaus.
evidence: Empirical hardness and adversarial generation for Hamiltonicity are established outside games.
limitation: Uses general graphs and one specialized solver; does not test a game-mechanic conjunction or matched Bloxorz variants.

work: A Framework for Generating Informative Benchmark Instances
method: Automatically generates graded instances or instances that discriminate between solving approaches.
evidence: Paper 2 cannot claim novelty from generating diagnostic/discriminating instances.
limitation: No game-mechanic semantics and no explicit matching of planning-vs-model-learning burdens.

work: Exploring the Feature Space of TSP Instances Using Quality Diversity
method: Uses quality diversity to generate TSP instances across feature space and expose solver-performance differences.
evidence: Hard-instance/instance-space generation with QD is established.
limitation: No counterfactual cross-mask interaction objective.

work: Toward Cooperative Level Generation in Multiplayer Games: A User Study in Overcooked!
method: Defines four cooperation patterns and a controllable level generator intended to induce diverse cooperation in two-player Overcooked.
evidence: Controllable cooperative-level generation and explicit cooperation-pattern targeting are already published.
limitation: Uses a specific game and human-facing cooperation patterns; does not establish policy-invariant formal content descriptors.

work: Verifying Maze-Like Game Levels With Model Checker SPIN
area: Formal verification + PCG + automated game testing
method: Full-text OA paper models maze, racing-maze and Sokoban-style behavior in PROMELA/SPIN, automatically tailors models to generated levels, uses counterexamples as winning action sequences, and reports five experiments including comparisons with A* and MCTS.
evidence: Procedural generation + formal model checking + automatic solution/witness generation and solver comparisons are established game-testing contributions.
limitation: Focus is level correctness/reachability in fixed behavioral templates, not causal failure attribution, mechanic interaction activation, or cross-game transfer.

work: Instance Space Analysis for Algorithm Testing: Methodology and Software Tools
method: Formalizes ISA for mapping instance features to algorithm performance, benchmark coverage and per-instance algorithm strengths/weaknesses.
evidence: Feature-based empirical hardness mapping and solver complementarity are mature methodology.
limitation: General methodology; not causal/theorem-informed game-mechanic activation.

work: Searching for Balanced 2D Brawler Games: Successes and Failures of Automated Evaluation
method: Shows optimization of an automated balance fitness function need not translate into the hypothesized human experience in user play.
evidence: Automated game-design metrics can optimize the wrong proxy even when numerically successful.
limitation: Human-alignment concern rather than evaluator-population mechanic attribution.

work: Plotting: A Planning Problem With Complex Transitions
method: Introduces a Plotting benchmark generator with 200 synthetic puzzle instances and compares SAT, CP, MIP and Fast Downward; reports strong horizon-dependent/phase-transition-like empirical difficulty and solver differences.
evidence: Generated game/puzzle instances plus multi-solver empirical hardness measurement is mature prior art.
limitation: Not driven by a complexity-theorem mechanic intervention and does not estimate causal interaction among game mechanics.

work: Regret Pruning for Learning Equilibria in Simulation-Based Games
method: Progressive sampling and regret-pruning reduce simulator queries while providing guarantees for approximate pure/mixed Nash equilibria of empirical games.
evidence: Query-efficient equilibrium inference from expensive simulators is also established.
limitation: Focuses sampling of fixed strategy profiles rather than game-design parameter optimization with generalizing neural surrogates.

work: The Legend of Zelda: The Complexity of Mechanics
method: Classifies many individual Zelda mechanics and combinations as polynomial, NP-hard/complete or PSPACE-hard/complete using multiple gadget frameworks.
evidence: A rich library of theorem-backed mechanic regimes exists inside one recognizable game family.
limitation: No systematic finite-instance empirical multi-solver study or matched intervention analysis.

work: A Taxonomy for Similarity Metrics between Markov Decision Processes
method: Systematizes MDP similarity metrics, model/performance viewpoints and their relation to transfer/generalization.
evidence: Confirms task similarity/transferability is a mature theory/method field.
limitation: Does not isolate human-readable game-mechanic changes.

work: SMACv2: An Improved Benchmark for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
method: Procedurally generated scenarios require generalization to unseen settings; corrects open-loop-policy weakness of SMAC.
evidence: Procedural cooperative benchmark generation is established on the agent-evaluation side.
limitation: Same-distribution scenario generalization; not cross-game content-side coordination descriptors.

work: Self-directed Learning of Action Models using Exploratory Planning
area: Active model learning / exploratory planning / game environment
method: An agent deliberately explores to learn action preconditions/effects without expert traces or a fixed goal, using planning to reach informative contexts. Evaluation includes an exploration-focused video-game scenario.
evidence: Active intervention/action selection for learning unknown mechanics/action models is already established and has a game evaluation.
limitation: Does not focus specifically on minimal cross-version behavioral witnesses for a known pair/family of candidate game versions.

work: Stateful Active Facilitator: Coordination and Environmental Heterogeneity in Cooperative MARL
method: Formalizes coordination level and heterogeneity level; HECOGrid provides quantitative control over both.
evidence: Scalar coordination-demand control in cooperative environments is already explicit.
limitation: Not a PCG benchmark across games/partner policies; primarily evaluates MARL algorithms.

work: The Game of Hidden Rules: A New Kind of Benchmark Challenge for Machine Learning
method: Expressive rule language enables fine controlled task changes to study how rule facets affect practical learning difficulty.
evidence: Fine-grained rule/task perturbation for ML difficulty is already an explicit benchmark goal.
limitation: Primarily hidden-rule learning, not general game-mechanic demand signatures or cross-algorithm mechanic causality.

work: Verifying Maze-Like Game Levels With Model Checker SPIN
method: Uses SPIN and counterexamples to verify maze-like levels and obtain winning action sequences.
evidence: Model checking for level solvability/property verification is established.
limitation: Domain templates/abstractions are needed; scalability depends on state-space size.

work: PSPACE-Completeness of Reversible Deterministic Systems
method: Develops a framework showing several fully reversible deterministic systems are PSPACE-complete, including deterministic constraint logic and reversible gadget systems. Thus even global reversibility/undoability does not imply tractability.
evidence: A broad causal story 'loss of reversibility makes games hard' is false as a general complexity claim.
limitation: Different systems/objectives and PSPACE regime; no finite matched mechanic experiment.

work: Policy Diagnosis via Measuring Role Diversity in Cooperative Multi-agent RL
method: Defines role diversity from action-, trajectory-, and contribution-based perspectives and links it to MARL policy performance.
evidence: A multidimensional cooperative-task characteristic is already formalized and tested on MPE/SMAC.
limitation: Policy/task diagnosis, not procedural content generation; does not define a portable PCG target representation.

work: Offline Meta Reinforcement Learning — Identifiability Challenges and Effective Data Collection Strategies
method: Formalizes MDP ambiguity/identifiability problems when tasks are inferred from fixed offline data and studies data-collection requirements.
evidence: Passive-data task/model identifiability is established theory.
limitation: Not game-mechanic semantic observability specifically.

work: Automated Generation of Initial Configurations for Testing Component Systems
method: Enumerates symmetry-free initial component configurations that satisfy architectural, consistency and user invariants, then uses them as starting configurations for online tests.
evidence: Correct-by-construction constrained initial-state/configuration generation for testing is established.
limitation: Component architectures rather than game content; objective is testing coverage/reconfiguration, not learned game-rule distinguishability.

work: Online Learning of Action Models for PDDL Planning
method: Learns PDDL action models during execution and plans toward informative states/action contexts where missing preconditions/effects can be discovered.
evidence: Planning-to-informative-states for action-model learning is established.
limitation: No game-level generation or learned GameCWM causal-fidelity target.

work: Proper Value Equivalence
method: Introduces proper value equivalence and shows multiple imperfect models can still be sufficient for optimal planning.
evidence: Further removes any novelty from treating exact transition recovery as unnecessary for decision making.
limitation: No mechanic-level causal comparison of learning burden versus search burden.

work: Heterogeneous Effects of Software Patches in a Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Game
area: Game patches / causal inference / heterogeneous player effects
method: Uses causal inference on League of Legends and shows that software patches affect players differently by skill level and break duration, with the performance gap between stronger and weaker players changing after patches.
evidence: Patch effects on player performance and skill strata are directly occupied.
limitation: Does not distinguish true ability adaptation from non-invariance of the performance/skill measurement function.

work: A Multifaceted Surrogate Model for Search-Based Procedural Content Generation
method: Learns mapping among levels, rules and gameplay outcomes; uses surrogate for search-based generation toward balance/match-duration targets.
evidence: Surrogate-guided game design and joint level/rules outcome modeling are mature.
limitation: Does not systematically test re-equilibrated strategic decision fidelity.

work: On the Importance of Environments in Human-Robot Coordination
method: Procedurally generates solvable Overcooked environments diverse with respect to coordination measures and shows qualitatively/statistically different coordination behavior even with the same planning algorithm.
evidence: Environment/content can already be optimized to induce diverse coordination measures; content→coordination is established.
limitation: Does not test whether a coordination descriptor remains invariant across substantially different partner-policy families or team sizes.

work: Asking the Right Questions: Learning Interpretable Action Models Through Query Answering
method: Introduces plan-outcome queries consisting of an initial state and an action plan; queries are synthesized to distinguish candidate STRIPS models, and candidate hypotheses are pruned from observed outcomes.
evidence: Choosing an initial state plus an action sequence to distinguish competing transition/action models is established peer-reviewed prior art.
limitation: Uses planning-domain states rather than game-level content grammars; AAAI experiments draw candidate initial states from random walks rather than studying level realizability as a scientific factor.

work: Synthesis of Static Test Environments for Observing Sequence-like Behaviors in Autonomous Systems
method: Synthesizes initial conditions and minimally constraining static environment restrictions so an autonomous system must exhibit target sequence-like behavior while completing its mission.
evidence: Environment/test-scenario synthesis beyond choosing actions is established formal-testing prior.
limitation: Autonomous-system behavior testing, not comparison of learned game-rule models; environment represented as graph constraints rather than game level grammar.

work: General Game Heuristic Prediction Based on Ludeme Descriptions
method: Uses Ludii game-description/ludeme features to predict heuristic performance across games.
evidence: Rule-description → AI performance prediction is established.
limitation: Heuristic prediction differs from component-specific policy/value transfer under controlled rule edits.

work: General Board Game Concepts
method: Defines hundreds of interpretable concepts derived from Ludii game descriptions, with intended uses including characterization, AI selection and transfer.
evidence: Creates an explicit semantic feature space for rule/game differences.
limitation: Concept existence does not itself establish which concept changes cause positive/negative transfer.

work: Distance-Based Mapping for General Game Playing
method: Introduces MMap/LMap approximations of distance/mappings between game rule graphs and evaluates transfer scenarios.
evidence: Game distance + mapping for transfer is directly established.
limitation: Not a signed mechanic-level negative-transfer attribution law.

work: General Board Game Concepts
method: Formalizes broad game concepts derived from Ludii ludemes for states, moves and games; motivates AI selection, transfer and explanation.
evidence: Interpretable mechanic/concept descriptors are available and should be reused rather than reinvented.
limitation: Does not estimate controlled mechanic interactions or empirical-hardness activation.

work: Toward Co-creative Dungeon Generation via Transfer Learning
method: Transfers a co-creative level-design model from Mario to Zelda dungeon rooms and fine-tunes transferred weights using approximated target-domain interaction data derived from Zelda rooms.
evidence: Learned generator transfer between quite distinct level domains is already demonstrated.
limitation: All transferred parameters remain trainable and substantial target-domain data are used; not zero-target/frozen.

work: A Phase Transition in Minesweeper
method: Empirically studies finite Minesweeper near a critical mine density; uses SAT/UNSAT reduction and grouped minimal unsatisfiable core size as a hardness metric; shows easy-hard-easy behavior and barriers for bounded inference methods.
evidence: Directly demonstrates that a theoretically hard game can exhibit structured finite-instance/average-case hardness regions.
limitation: Single game and density axis; not controlled activation/ablation of complexity-bearing mechanics across games or genuinely distinct solver families.

work: Modelling Behavioural Diversity for Learning in Open-Ended Games
method: Provides geometric behavioural-diversity interpretation and DPP metric; maximizing it enlarges the gamescape.
evidence: Strategic diversity and gamescape geometry are mature enough that a new diversity metric is risky.
limitation: Focus is learning diverse agent populations rather than causal effects of mechanics on strategic structure.

work: Fingerprinting Tabletop Games
method: Builds visual game fingerprints from repeated optimization of MCTS parameters and uses them to compare tabletop games.
evidence: The phrase and core idea of computational 'game fingerprinting' are already directly occupied.
limitation: MCTS-centric and based on optimized algorithm parameters rather than causal mechanic interventions or multi-resource counterfactuals.

work: General Game Heuristic Prediction Based on Ludeme Descriptions
method: Predicts performance of general-game-playing heuristics from Ludii game descriptions and analyzes ludemes defining games.
evidence: Rule/ludeme descriptions have already been used to predict algorithm performance.
limitation: Observational corpus prediction, not controlled mechanic interventions, interaction terms or worst-case-vs-empirical-hardness analysis.

work: Visualizing Multiplayer Game Spaces
method: Embeds multiplayer board games into several game-spaces, including statistics from repeated MCTS parameter optimization; shows algorithmic game-space is interpretable and differs from simple game-tree attributes.
evidence: Using optimized AI behavior/parameters to characterize and compare games is an established research line.
limitation: Does not isolate causal effects of individual mechanics or define cross-solver resource-response estimands.

work: Transfer of Fully Convolutional Policy-Value Networks Between Games and Game Variants
method: Uses shared semantic channels in Ludii to transfer AlphaZero-like networks between variants and distinct board games, including zero-shot tests.
evidence: Cross-game transfer using formal/shared game semantics is established on PLAYER policy networks.
limitation: Not interpretable symbolic concepts; not procedural designer transfer.

work: Heterogeneous Effects of Software Patches in a Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Game
area: Patch effects / causal inference / player heterogeneity
method: Studies League of Legends software patches with causal/quasi-experimental methods and finds heterogeneous responses associated with player skill and time away from the game, showing that one patch can affect player strata differently.
evidence: Heterogeneous player response to live-game patches is empirically established.
limitation: Focuses behavioral/player outcomes rather than strategic balance-region deformation or robust parameter selection.

work: Reward Machines for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
method: Reward-machine decomposition explicitly encodes teammate interdependencies/independencies and verifiable task decomposition.
evidence: Formal structural representation of cooperative dependence is established.
limitation: A learning/task-decomposition method, not a content-generation benchmark.

work: Softlock Detection for Super Metroid with Computation Tree Logic
method: Uses CTL on a gameplay abstraction to detect non-obvious softlocks and turn counterexamples into explanations.
evidence: Formal softlock detection and counterexample explanation in games are established.
limitation: Requires compact enumerable abstraction; transfer to arbitrary games is nontrivial.

work: ERMAS: Becoming Robust to Reward Function Sim-to-Real Gaps in Multi-Agent Simulations
area: Robust multi-agent simulation / economic policy / sim-to-real
method: Defines epsilon-robust multi-agent simulation against uncertainty in agents' reward functions and worst-case epsilon-equilibria. In AI-Economist taxation experiments, robust policies tolerate changes in agent risk aversion and can improve social welfare.
evidence: Robust policy design against behavioral/reward misspecification in multi-agent economic simulations is already a formal methodology.
limitation: Not video-game economy balancing specifically, but it removes generic 'robust to player behavior shift' as a method novelty.

work: Benchmarking the Spectrum of Agent Capabilities (Crafter)
method: Single open-world survival game evaluates achievements requiring exploration, long-term reasoning and generalization.
evidence: Broad capability benchmarking inside a game is established.
limitation: Agent-centric; achievement set does not estimate intrinsic game demand by controlled capability interventions.
